# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group focused on governance frameworks, risk management, and regulatory compliance for agentic AI technologies[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group establishes operational conventions for meeting records, tracking AI summaries, transcripts, topics discussed, formal decisions, deliverables, and action items[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee (TC)
proposed_concept.description: The governing body responsible for reviewing project proposals, recommending projects, and applying the project lifecycle policy for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) assists the Governing Board (GB) of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by reviewing new project proposals, recommending projects that align with the AAIF mission, and applying the Project Lifecycle Policy to Technical Projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
The TC is composed of one representative appointed by each Platinum Member of AAIF [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

Key responsibilities include:
1. Establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups (WGs) relevant to AAIF's scope.
2. Coordinating collaboration between Technical Projects and developing overall technical priorities.
3. Recommending projects to the GB for acceptance as Technical Projects.
4. Deciding changes in a Technical Project’s status within the Lifecycle Policy.
5. Applying and maintaining the Lifecycle Policy, subject to GB approval [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

Decisions are primarily consensus-based. If a vote is required, it operates on a one-vote-per-voting-member basis. Quorum requires 50% of voting members. Decisions can also be made via lazy consensus, where a proposal is approved if no formal objection is recorded within 72 hours [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
The TC Charter was adopted on March 3, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group (GRR WG)
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group focusing on landscape analysis, gap analysis, and distilled guidance related to governance, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group (GRR WG) addresses governance frameworks, risk assessment, and regulatory considerations relevant to agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. The group operates on a biweekly cadence [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Architecture / Specification
The GRR WG adopted a three-step working model for its deliverables:
1. Landscape analysis of existing standards, frameworks, regulations (e.g., GDPR, EU AI Act, eIDAS 2), and use cases [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
2. Gap analysis identifying where current approaches fail to address emerging agentic AI risks [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. Distilled guidance/principles for organizations, pending a decision on the scope boundary for implementation guidance [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

Initial deliverables include problem set statements for governance and regulatory challenges, and the consolidated landscape analysis [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. The group also plans to develop candidate risk-assessment/protocol concepts for agent-human oversight interactions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

Collaboration primarily uses a shared Google Doc, with Discord as a secondary channel [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its kickoff meeting on 2026-02-19 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. By 2026-03-05, the group aligned on its three-step deliverable model [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning standards and developing conventions for agent-level observability, workflow tracing, and cross-framework telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to build a shared understanding of agent observability, align telemetry efforts, identify gaps, and produce guidance or specifications across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. It operates within the foundation under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Working Group Lifecycle](../governance/working-group-lifecycle.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Scope and Activities
The working group acts primarily as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards organization, coordinating upstream with bodies like the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

Key areas of focus include:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Expanding beyond isolated LLM call tracing to capture session- and workflow-level agent behavior across multiple turns, tool calls, and model invocations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Cross-Framework Interoperability**: Establishing vendor- and framework-neutral conventions so observability tools and agent runtimes can discover agents and exchange trace data without proprietary lock-in[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Auditability and Accountability**: Providing lineage, fidelity, and grounding traces for complex multimodal and tool-augmented workflows to support evaluation, debugging, and compliance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Governance
The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and coordinates internally with adjacent foundation efforts including the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Case Study Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines and requirements for AAIF member organizations publishing written or webinar case studies on open agentic AI implementations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Case Study Guidelines outline the standards, formats, and review processes for Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) member organizations sharing real-world implementations of foundation technologies and standards[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

# Strategic Focus and Structure
Case studies must demonstrate measurable business impact resulting from the adoption of open agentic AI standards such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, or AGENTS.md[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

Core evaluation themes include:
- **Agentic Maturity**: Progressing from basic conversational interfaces to autonomous, goal-directed agent systems[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].
- **Interoperability**: Implementing seamless integrations across heterogeneous models, environments, and tooling via open specifications[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].
- **Measurable Acceleration**: Documenting quantitative benefits such as reduced resolution time, cost reductions, or higher operational throughput[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

# Submission Formats
Members can participate via two primary mechanisms[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]:
1. **Written Case Studies**: Structured narratives covering organizational context, technical and business challenges, solution architecture, and verified business outcomes.
2. **Webinar Case Studies**: Recorded 20–30 minute presentations with interactive Q&A hosted across foundation channels.

mutations.rationale: Document the AAIF Agentic AI Landscape initiative, generation mechanism, and project inclusion guidelines from the landscape repository documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: An interactive landscape cataloging open source software, open standards, and member projects across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive overview of the agentic AI ecosystem, cataloging prominent open source software, open standards, and AAIF member projects.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] It is built using the CNCF Landscape2 tooling and generated on a daily cadence from repository configuration data.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

# Architecture / Specification
Entries in the landscape are maintained in `landscape.yml` and must satisfy specific submission guidelines:[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

- **Project Eligibility**: Open source projects generally require at least 1,000 GitHub stars and must clearly fit into an existing landscape category.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Scope Restrictions**: Commercial distributions of open source software, closed-source products and services, and proprietary standards are excluded, as are closed-source products that implement open source solutions.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Categorization Rules**: An organization's offerings are typically listed in only one category box representing their major or best-known project.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Asset Requirements**: Logos must be provided in SVG format, include the project or company name in English, use stacked layouts when multiple variants exist, and avoid reversed or non-transparent backgrounds.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **Metadata Fields**: Projects define metadata such as controlling Crunchbase organization mappings and optional details via CNCF Landscape2 `extra` fields.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines defining expected behavior, unacceptable behavior, and enforcement procedures for participation in the AAIF community.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes guidelines for fostering an inclusive, welcoming, and safe environment across all Foundation activities, including technical projects, events, and communication channels [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

The Code applies to Governing Board, Technical Committee, Working Group, and Outreach Committee meetings, as well as any other AAIF activity not covered by a specific technical project's code of conduct. Events produced with professional staff are governed by the LF Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this document. Technical projects under the AAIF umbrella maintain their own codes of conduct [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Expected Behavior

Community members are expected to use welcoming and inclusive language, respect differing viewpoints, accept constructive criticism, prioritize community benefit, show empathy, and be professional and responsible in all interactions [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Unacceptable Behavior

Unacceptable behaviors include harassment and discrimination (verbal, physical, visual, sexual harassment, stalking), inappropriate communication (sexualized language/imagery, violent language, trolling, personal attacks), and publishing private information without permission [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Enforcement

Violations can be reported to the designated contacts. Consequences for violations range from warnings to temporary or permanent exclusion from the community [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skill Format
proposed_concept.description: A portable bundle of instructions, references, scripts, and assets that provides reusable expertise for compatible AI agents based on the Agent Skills specification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Skills are defined as portable bundles of instructions, references, scripts, and assets that help AI agents perform specialized tasks. A skill provides an agent with reusable expertise for a specific domain, workflow, brand, tool, or process [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

The format follows the external Agent Skills specification [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification

Each skill resides in its own directory containing a `SKILL.md` file, which includes YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions. Supporting files may include:

*   `assets/`: Images, logos, templates, or static resources.
*   `references/`: Longer documentation or reference material.
*   `scripts/`: Executable helper scripts [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

Agents compatible with the format (e.g., goose, claude code, codex, gemini) can load skills on demand based on context, such as when a prompt references a specific skill or domain [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

mutations.rationale: The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the core values (Neutral, Collaborative, Trustworthy) that govern all branded content creation.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Foundation Principles
proposed_concept.description: The core values—Neutral, Collaborative, and Trustworthy—that guide the creation of all visual and written content for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Foundation defines the core identity and values that the Foundation seeks to communicate through its visuals, presentations, documents, and marketing materials. The brand should feel neutral, collaborative, and trustworthy, communicating open governance, shared ownership, and credible infrastructure for the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

# Architecture / Specification

The foundation is built upon three core principles:

## Neutral
AAIF governance is designed so no single vendor controls the ecosystem. Decisions are transparent, standards are developed collectively, and the work belongs to everyone. This implies avoiding visual treatments that suggest ownership by one company, favoring open and standards-oriented framing, and avoiding hype or exclusivity [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

## Collaborative
AAIF unites diverse perspectives and resources from industry leaders to build what no single organization could own alone. This requires emphasizing cooperation, shared standards, and ecosystem building, using inclusive language like “shared,” “collective,” and “community,” and avoiding individualistic framing [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

## Trustworthy
The brand is built on the Linux Foundation’s reputation for neutrality and principled governance, providing the credibility and stability needed for open-source projects. This mandates a confident, clear, and grounded tone, preferring precise claims over broad hype, and using clean, professional compositions [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

proposed_concept.description: A repository hosting portable bundles of instructions and assets (Agent Skills) developed by AAIF to provide reusable expertise for compatible AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Public Agent Skills repository is an initiative dedicated to collecting and distributing Agent Skills developed by the Foundation. Agent Skills are defined as portable bundles of instructions, references, scripts, and assets that help AI agents perform specialized tasks [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification

The repository structure organizes skills into individual directories, each containing a `SKILL.md` file that adheres to the [Agent Skill Format](../specification/agent-skill.md) [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

Examples of skills hosted include the `aaif-brand-guidelines` skill, which applies the Foundation's brand principles to content creation [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

Users can install and manage these skills using the Skills CLI [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

proposed_concept.title: Public Agents Initiative
proposed_concept.description: A repository hosting public, reusable agent assets including skills, recipes, prompts, and inference workflows for AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Public Agents initiative provides a centralized repository (`aaif/public-agents`) containing public, reusable agent resources for the Agentic AI Foundation, including agent skills, recipes, prompts, and agent-facing workflows[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Repository Structure
The repository organizes agent assets into standardized directories[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]:
- `skills/`: [Agent Skills](../specification/agent-skill.md) offering reusable domain expertise, brand guidance, workflows, and tool instructions (such as the AAIF brand guidelines skill)[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7][^evt-public-agents-pr-1].
- `recipes/`: Repeatable agent workflows and task definitions[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `prompts/`: Reusable prompts and prompt templates[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `docs/`: Supporting documentation for contributors and consumers[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Inference and Testing Workflows
The repository maintains workflow automation in `.github/workflows/` for testing LLM API integration:
- `copilot-test-action`: Queries the GitHub Models catalog and executes inference via the org endpoint using the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`[^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f][^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `gemini-test-action`: Calls the Google Gemini API directly using a repository secret `GEMINI_API_KEY`[^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626][^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security threat models, shared taxonomies, protocol privacy reviews, and design patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security and privacy threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and distilled guidance across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.

# Charter and Governance
The working group presented its charter to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in April 2026, proceeding with operations and workstream formation following initial consensus[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Key Focus Areas and Workstreams
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy Collaboration**: Providing the foundational draft taxonomy to seed the joint cross-working-group taxonomy effort across all AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security and Privacy Analysis**: Tracking extensions to the Model Context Protocol (MCP), including MCP Interceptors (hooks for redaction and privacy) and MCP Apps (evaluating UI trust boundaries)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Operating Model**: Transitioning towards distributed, self-organized async workstreams supported by cadence check-in meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

mutations.rationale: Add the Identity & Trust Working Group established to address agent identity, authentication, delegation, and cross-organizational trust models.

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group identifying and promoting standards for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its purpose is to ensure agents can be discovered across platforms, prove who they are and who they act for, represent what human approvals occurred, and operate under auditable constraints across organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on core areas of agentic interaction and authority [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: How agents are uniquely identified, how they authenticate, and how they convey their origin, operating entity, and software context [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Mechanisms representing an agent acting on behalf of a human, role, service, or process, including the scope and limits of delegated power [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, policy constraints, and human consent or approval controls [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: How independent systems reason about whether an incoming external agent is authentic and authorized to act [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Agent Discovery and Metadata**: Discovery protocols and trust-relevant metadata that interface with observability and traceability frameworks [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

## Boundary and Scope Limits
The working group does not ratify formal standards on behalf of standards development organizations, nor does it define general security execution controls or build production identity infrastructure [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Security threat modeling and runtime architectures are coordinated with the [Security & Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) and related foundation initiatives [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning standards and developing conventions for agent-level observability, workflow tracing, and cross-framework auditability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to bring together practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to develop a shared understanding and vendor-neutral conventions for agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

Operating as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards organization, the group focuses on aligning existing telemetry efforts, identifying gaps, and producing specifications or upstream contributions where existing bodies do not meet agentic workflow needs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

### Mission and Operating Principles
The working group adheres to the core principle of "coordinate first, specify only when necessary" [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Its primary goals include:
- Addressing fragmented observability across proprietary platforms (such as LangSmith, Arize, and AgentOps) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- Bridging the gap between individual LLM call tracing (e.g., OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, OpenInference, OpenLLMetry) and multi-turn, multi-tool workflow and session-level agent behavior [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- Establishing lineage, fidelity, and grounding trace standards for multi-modal agentic workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

### Focus Areas
The WG operates under a Focus Area model, with its founding focus area designated as the **Agent Behavior Trace Model** [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Governance and Leadership

- **Charter Approval Date:** 2026-05-13 (Ratified: 2026-04-15) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **Primary Contact / Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **Coordination:** Collaborates internally across AAIF groups and externally with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

mutations.rationale: Update working group concept with formal scope, mission, and leadership details from the approved charter.

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, agent containment patterns, and data protection practices across the ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to establish security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

The group produces open threat models, shared taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that agent providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to maintain trustworthy agentic deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification

### Mission and Scope
SPAA addresses agent-specific risks such as prompt injection, confused deputy issues, authorization boundary violations, tool invocation vulnerabilities, and agent memory exploitation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

In-scope activities include:
- Threat modeling and attack analysis [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Security architecture and reusable design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Agent control, guardrails, and containment mechanisms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Data protection, data lifecycle, and privacy controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

### Out of Scope
To avoid domain overlap, the charter explicitly excludes:
- Ethics, bias, and normative value judgments (deferred to the Governance, Risk & Regulatory WG / Governance and Policy) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Interpreting or prescribing legal and regulatory compliance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Formal certification programs for agentic systems or tools [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Governance and Leadership

- **Charter Approval Date:** 2026-05-13 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **Primary Contact / Chair:** Alex Frazer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **Internal Coordination:** Works alongside [Governance, Risk & Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) and other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

proposed_concept.description: Content intake policy, contributor rules, and editorial standards for publishing vendor-neutral content on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Blog Guidelines establish the content intake process, editorial criteria, and submission workflow for publishing articles, project releases, and thought leadership on aaif.io [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

The Linux Foundation team oversees the publishing pipeline to ensure all published material is educational, timely, narrative, and vendor-neutral [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

### Contributor Eligibility and Content Rules
Submissions are accepted from member companies, project maintainers, working groups, the [Technical Committee](technical-committee.md), event participants, and community contributors [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Core requirements include:
- **Vendor Neutrality:** Content must not promote one member over others or act as sales collateral. Member companies are restricted to one or two closing sentences with a single external link [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Focus:** High-value topics include updates on AAIF-hosted projects (MCP, goose, AGENTS.md), technical tutorials, interoperability patterns, and real-world case studies [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Originality & Timeliness:** Posts must be original, unpublished elsewhere, and reflect work from within the last two months [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Frequency:** Community contributors are permitted up to two posts per month [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

### Agent Skill Automation
Contributors can prepare and review blog submissions using the `aaif-blog-guidelines` [agent skill](../specification/agent-skill.md) available in [Public Agents](../initiatives/public-agents.md) [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2]:

```bash
npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill aaif-blog-guidelines --global
```

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, agent containment patterns, and security architecture guidance for the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy (S&P) Working Group is dedicated to establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem, focusing on pre-competitive collaboration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The WG addresses risks inherent in multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation, delegated authentication, and agent memory [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The WG operates biweekly, driven by consensus, with GitHub used for tracking and notes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification
The scope includes threat modeling, security architecture, agent control/containment, data protection, and cross-WG collaboration. Explicitly out-of-scope are ethics/bias, regulatory compliance interpretation, and certification [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

A key focus area is standardizing "hooks" mechanisms, which have emerged as a universal concern across related efforts like MCP Interceptors and ACS specifications, aiming to define behavior for checkpoints and human-in-the-loop interventions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Deliverables
The WG has defined several initial deliverables, sequenced to build upon each other [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:
1. Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design: A near-term deliverable intended to identify gaps in existing threat models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
2. Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist: A checklist intended for early socialization with other WG chairs to ensure security and privacy considerations are integrated across AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
3. Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog: A technical guide defining concrete patterns (e.g., hooks, checkpoints) and anti-patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
4. Agentic Security Best Practices Guide: A higher-level advisory guide paired with the Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
The WG coordinates with external standards bodies like AARM and internal groups like the MCP Apps and ACS specification groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape, also referred to as the "AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map," is a dynamic, interactive market map built using the CNCF Landscape 2 tooling[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

The landscape aims to provide visibility into the ecosystem, covering agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and global regulatory regimes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape uses the CNCF Landscape 2 specification, requiring validation of `landscape.yml` (data) and `settings.yml` (configuration) files[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].

Key structural components include:
1. **Project Tiers:** Projects are categorized into Graduated, Incubating, Member, and External tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
2. **Project Watchlist:** A section dedicated to tracking top agentic AI open source projects, which can be synchronized with the Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard on LFX Insights[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
3. **Grouping:** The structure decouples AAIF Members from Projects, allowing for highlighting of AAIF member projects within the map[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

Pull requests modifying the landscape data or settings trigger a preview workflow, allowing contributors to view changes before merging[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

proposed_concept.title: Social Media Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Governance and guidelines for content strategy, official reposting, and community content amplification across AAIF social channels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) social media content strategy, account access, and brand compliance are led by the Linux Foundation staff to ensure neutral, professional, and consistent ecosystem communication[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. Social platforms serve to broadcast official Foundation-wide updates, milestones, releases, events, and initiatives across the open source AI ecosystem[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

# Architecture / Specification

### Content Baselines
AAIF social channels maintain a neutral, inclusive, and professional tone aligned with foundational brand values[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637] (see [../governance/brand-foundation.md](brand-foundation.md)):
- **Relevance**: All posts, shares, and replies must focus on open-source agentic AI, community events, or learning resources[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
- **No Unsolicited Promotions**: Generic self-promotions, advertisements, product announcements, and sponsored content are prohibited[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
- **Attribution**: Proper attribution must be given for shared code or ideas while respecting open source licenses[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
- **Platform Alignment**: Content is tailored across platforms, utilizing X for concise announcements, LinkedIn for professional case studies and technical discussions, and Bluesky for conversational community engagement[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

### Content Submission and Amplification
Community members and organizations can request social amplification through two designated channels[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:
1. **Direct Reposts**: Submitted through the designated AAIF Discord social amplification channel[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. Reposts are limited to official project releases, working group announcements, official events, and community projects explicitly implementing AAIF standards[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
2. **Organic AAIF Posts**: Submitted via the AAIF Content Intake Form for structured review and scheduling by Foundation staff[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications and reference architectures for agent-driven commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) catalogs, aligns, and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. The group operates as a protocol-neutral forum providing interoperability guidance, transaction reference models, and recommendations to the Technical Committee rather than authoring competing commerce protocols[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification

### Working Group Scope
The Working Group focuses on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and commerce ecosystems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Agent–merchant interfaces for catalog offers, availability, dynamic terms, and fulfillment options[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Cart state composition, validation, and checkout handoff between autonomous agents and merchant platforms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity verification, authority scoping, and consent conveyance in collaboration with the Identity & Trust Working Group (see [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](identity-and-trust.md))[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Signaling interfaces across agents, digital wallets, and payment rails (cards, real-time, on-chain) for intent, authorization, and settlement[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling**: Exchange of risk-posture signals between agents, merchants, and risk management systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Autonomy Boundaries & Human Oversight**: Escalation policies, confirmation patterns, and representation of autonomous authority limits[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Post-Purchase Interfaces**: Signals for order-status tracking, dispute initiation, claims, and chargebacks[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### Scope Boundaries
The WG explicitly excludes operational mechanics and internal implementations of underlying payment rails, fraud engines, and identity providers[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. It also excludes end-user hardware, consumer UI design, general non-agentic commerce governance, and proprietary protocol development[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15**: Charter approved and ratified under leads Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: The policy governing intake requirements, stage progression (Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual reviews for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy sets forth the formal process for open technical projects to join the Foundation, progress through maturity stages, and undergo periodic review[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Administered by the Technical Committee (see [../governance/technical-committee.md](technical-committee.md)), the framework enables projects to participate at the stage suited to their development while providing access to foundation mentorship, infrastructure, and cross-project alignment[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification

### Project Proposal Requirements
Proposals for new or incoming projects are submitted to the `aaif/project-proposals` repository and must document[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Project identity, origin history, and problem statement[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Alignment with the AAIF mission and integration with existing Foundation initiatives[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Adoption evidence and reference use cases[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Permissive OSI-approved licensing and public repository location[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- CI/CD automation, public validation suites, and public release processes[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Public issue tracking and formal contribution guidelines[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- External project dependencies and their respective licenses[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Governance documentation (`GOVERNANCE.md`), core maintainer lists, and decision-making processes[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Communication channels, financial sponsorships, and requested infrastructure support[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

### Lifecycle Stages
Projects enter and move through three formal stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
1. **Growth Stage**: Designed for early-stage or rapidly evolving projects showing promise, active contribution, and clear alignment with foundation priorities[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
2. **Impact Stage**: For mature, production-ready projects with widespread ecosystem adoption, robust multi-organization governance, and sustained maintenance[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
3. **Emeritus Stage**: For retired, deprecated, or legacy projects that have completed their lifecycle or are no longer actively maintained[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171, ^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

### Annual Review Process
All active projects undergo an Annual Review by the Technical Committee to evaluate community health, adoption trends, license compliance, and progression between stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-18**: Project Lifecycle Policy formally enacted[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **2026-03-24**: Textual fixes and issue template adjustments applied in PR #30[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Lifecycle and Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Process for member submission, evaluation, establishment, and operational lifecycle of AAIF Working Groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Working Groups are structured, time-bound collaborations of subject matter experts convened by the Agentic AI Foundation to advance research, develop interoperability standards, and produce actionable guidance across agentic AI systems[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. The lifecycle and intake process governs how working group proposals are authored, submitted by Foundation members, reviewed by the Technical Committee (see [../governance/technical-committee.md](technical-committee.md)), and managed through charter cycles[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification

### Submission Eligibility
Working Group idea submissions are open exclusively to AAIF member organizations in good standing across all membership tiers[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Submissions from entities outside the Foundation membership are not reviewed[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

### Proposal Requirements
Proposals submitted via the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository must contain eight key sections[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Name, affiliation, contact email, proposed leadership capacity, and membership tier[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
2. **Working Group Identity**: Clear group name and an accessible one-sentence summary without jargon[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Specific agentic AI challenges addressed and strategic alignment with AAIF goals[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Boundaries and tangible outputs such as technical whitepapers, specifications, benchmarks, datasets, or policy frameworks[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Meeting cadence and duration (typically chartered on 12–24 month cycles)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Required stakeholder perspectives and initial commitments from interested organizations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Assessment of ecosystem necessity and timeliness[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
8. **Resource Considerations**: Foundation infrastructure or tooling requirements[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

### Review and Code of Conduct
All proposal reviews follow the standard review process evaluated against alignment, feasibility, and deliverable clarity under the Foundation's Code of Conduct (see [../governance/code-of-conduct.md](code-of-conduct.md))[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a, ^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, shared taxonomies, agent containment patterns, and security best practices.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG) is responsible for establishing standards, best practices, and frameworks related to securing agentic AI systems and ensuring user privacy. The WG charter was formally approved on 2026-05-26, making the group fully legitimate [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Deliverables

The WG has defined several key deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:

*   **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A framework design effort involving approximately 11 volunteers, overlapping closely with the cross-WG Taxonomy/Landscape work.
*   **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: A broad scope guide drawing the largest interest from contributors.
*   **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A catalog of reusable patterns, which may require scope or timeline adjustment due to fewer volunteers.
*   **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**.

# Architecture / Specification

The WG contributes a security/privacy lens to the shared data defined by the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape workstream](../specification/taxonomy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History

Leadership structure is determined by self-selection within workstream channels, rather than assignment from initial surveys. Leads are expected to keep conversation moving, own status updates, and delegate work [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: The policy governing intake requirements, stage progression (Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review for foundation-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

This policy outlines the requirements and governance path for open source projects seeking to become foundation-hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Projects are classified into stages such as Growth or Impact.

# Application Process

Applicants must first review the policy documentation and then submit a Project Proposal Application via the designated issue form [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Applicants are encouraged to review guidance on submission criteria [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

Once submitted, the application is triaged and placed in the backlog. The applicant prepares a review presentation with staff assistance and the project is scheduled for review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) (TC) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Review and Voting

Project applications are reviewed and voted on by the AAIF Technical Committee (TC). The TC classifies the project as either **Growth** or **Impact**. Acceptance requires an **absolute majority vote (>50%)** of all members of the Technical Committee, followed by referral to the Governing Board for final approval [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

Projects that are declined may reapply after addressing issues raised during review, permitted as soon as three months after the declined vote if tangible progress has been made [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Status Labels

Applications progress through defined statuses [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| `New` | The application is new and placed in the backlog. |
| `Approved` | The application has been accepted into the foundation-hosted project structure. |
| `Declined` | The application has been declined. |
| `Waiting on Comment` | Additional information is required. |
| `Too Early` | The project is not yet ready. |

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the governing body responsible for reviewing project proposals, recommending projects, and applying governance policies across the foundation.

# Project Review and Voting

The TC reviews project applications during scheduled meetings. The TC is responsible for classifying accepted projects as either **Growth** or **Impact** projects [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

To be accepted, a project must receive an **absolute majority vote (>50%)** of all members of the Technical Committee. Following a successful TC vote, the project is referred to the Governing Board for final approval [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

2.  **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Aligns with [Identity & Trust WG](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
3.  **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Aligns with [Security & Privacy WG](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).
4.  **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Aligns with [Observability & Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
5.  **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Aligns with [Agentic Commerce WG](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).
6.  **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Aligns with [Governance, Risk & Regulatory WG](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
7.  **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Aligns with [Accuracy & Reliability WG](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) acts as a collaborative bridge between evolving global AI policy frameworks and technical developments in agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. Led by Ryan Hagemann (IBM), the group focuses on establishing shared understandings of risk mitigation, tracking regulatory movements, and closing standards gaps that hinder open source interoperability [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope and Focus Areas

The working group addresses governance challenges across several domains [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]:

- **Policy and Regulatory Monitoring**: Tracking emerging global AI regulations, standards, and compliance frameworks affecting agentic systems.
- **Protocol Governance**: Analyzing how open protocols (such as MCP) interface with organizational governance frameworks.
- **Future Standards Initiatives**: Exploring AI Agent Bill of Materials (A-BOM) standards, action reversibility and undo infrastructure, human-in-the-loop patterns, autonomy classifications, and incident reporting guidelines.
- **Cross-Ecosystem Alignment**: Integrating external domain frameworks (e.g., FINOS AI Governance Framework) with general agentic standards.

### Out of Scope

The GRRA WG does not provide formal legal advice, compliance solutions, or commercial product endorsements [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-01**: Working group charter drafted and submitted for review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-1] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, defense architectures, containment patterns, and privacy standards for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. The group operates through specialized workstreams that coordinate closely with the broader foundation and cross-cutting initiatives like the [Taxonomy Initiative](../specification/taxonomy.md) and [Agentic AI Landscape](../initiatives/agentic-ai-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Architecture / Specification

### Active Workstreams and Leadership

The working group organizes its technical deliverables into four core workstreams alongside cross-foundation delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:

- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, delivering standardized checklists for other AAIF groups to evaluate security considerations in emerging specifications.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, outlining operational guidelines for securing agent runtimes and tools.
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, identifying novel attack vectors (e.g., prompt injection, tool attestation vulnerabilities) and agent threat models.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, cataloging architectural containment and safety patterns.
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Delegates**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent the working group within the cross-WG terminology efforts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-09**: Workstream co-leads confirmed and cross-WG taxonomy delegates appointed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Lifecycle and Submission Policy
proposed_concept.description: Process for member submission, evaluation, Technical Committee voting, and operational establishment of AAIF Working Groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Lifecycle policy governs how new working groups are proposed, triaged, evaluated, and established under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. New working groups are initiated via public proposal templates and are reviewed and voted on by the [Technical Committee](./technical-committee.md) before final Governing Board approval [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Architecture / Specification

### Submission and Triage Process

1. **Application**: Proposers open a Working Group Proposal issue form in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
2. **Backlog & Triage**: Submitted proposals are placed on the Working Group Proposals project board for initial triage.
3. **TC Review**: Proposals are scheduled for discussion during regular Technical Committee meetings [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

### Voting Requirements

- To be approved, a working group proposal requires a **simple majority vote** of all members of the Technical Committee [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- Accepted proposals remain subject to final approval by the AAIF Governing Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

### Lifecycle Status Labels

Proposals are tracked using standard status labels [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `New` | Proposal submitted and placed in the triage backlog. |
| `Approved` | Proposal accepted by the TC and ready for establishment. |
| `Declined` | Proposal rejected, with rationales documented in issue comments. |
| `Waiting on Comment` | Reviewers requested additional information from submitters. |
| `Too Early` | Proposal requires further maturity or community validation prior to reapplication. |

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, security review checklists, design patterns, and best practices for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, security review checklists, reusable design patterns, and practical implementation guidance for agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). Serving as a cross-cutting security layer across AAIF initiatives, the working group addresses unique agentic risks including multi-agent persuasion, delegated authority boundaries, tool invocation risks, runtime containment, and prompt and tool supply-chain integrity.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output into dedicated workstreams and cross-cutting deliverables:

## Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
Evaluates existing AI threat modeling frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) to determine coverage of agentic-specific threat surfaces such as delegated authorization boundaries, tool invocation risks, multi-agent persuasion, and supply chain integrity (e.g., prompt integrity and tool manifest verification)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The output feeds directly into the Design Patterns Catalog and Best Practices Guide.
- **Leads:** Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]

## Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
Curates reusable architecture patterns documented in a problem, context, solution, and trade-offs format alongside corresponding anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Topics include:
- Hooks and checkpointing
- Human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns
- Privacy-preserving execution (Zero-Knowledge proofs, Trusted Execution Environments, encrypted vector databases)
- Blast radius containment
- Secure memory and memory lifecycle management (retention, deletion, data sovereignty)
- Agent containment and runtime intervention (kill switches, rollback mechanisms, permission downgrading, off-task detection)
- Agent authorization models
- **Leads:** Dan Kommatas (Circle), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]

## Security Best Practices Guide
Provides actionable, higher-level implementation guidance and pointers to external security frameworks for developers and operators building agentic workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Topics encompass secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrail implementation, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
- **Leads:** Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

## Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist
Defines a lightweight review checklist and process to assess deliverables across AAIF working groups through a security and privacy lens[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Initial target areas include:
- [Identity and Trust](./identity-and-trust.md): Agent identity, attestation, and delegated authorization
- [Observability and Traceability](./observability-and-traceability.md): Behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging
- [Agentic Commerce](./agentic-commerce.md): Payments security guardrails, fund draining prevention, account leakage mitigation, and payment-agent scope boundaries
- **Lead:** Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

## Taxonomy Workstream Integration
The working group previously maintained an independent terminology workstream, which was merged into the foundation-wide [Taxonomy](../specification/taxonomy.md) effort to ensure standard definitions across all working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Working Group Delegates:** Jay White (Microsoft), Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate newly established workstreams, threat modeling gap analysis deliverables, public repository status, and taxonomy delegates.

# Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical activities into several distinct workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Gap analysis of existing AI security frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threats such as memory and context poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, excessive agency, blast radius containment, and rogue agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable secure and privacy-preserving design patterns presented in a problem/context/solution/trade-offs format [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Best Practices Guide**: High-level guidance for builders alongside curated external references and recommendations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: A lightweight review process and checklist for evaluating deliverables from other AAIF working groups through a security and privacy lens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Taxonomy Delegation**: The working group's initial terminology draft transitioned to the cross-WG [Taxonomy specification](../specification/taxonomy.md) effort led by Junjie Bu, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy draft elevated to a foundation-wide initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Working group appointed delegates to the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Repositories made public; GitHub adopted as the system of record for maturing deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy specification is an AAIF-wide initiative maintained in the `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository to define a shared vocabulary and resolve conflicting definitions across working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Led by Junjie Bu, the initiative gathers 10 to 20 core domain terms from each working group into a unified foundation-wide taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy aligns cross-functional terminology across AAIF domains:
- **Cross-Working Group Representation**: Working groups appoint delegates (such as Jay White and Katherine Druckman from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) to reconcile domain terms and review candidate entries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **Working Group Term Harmonization**: Participating groups such as the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) review core terms and structured topic slices [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Agent Archetypes**: Classification framework proposed to map agent types based on distinct capabilities such as tool use and network access [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-12**: Began as an internal deliverable of the Security and Privacy WG before being elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed to lead the cross-WG workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Dedicated repository established at `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

mutations.rationale: Add focus group tracks, landscape surveys, public repository status, and Technical Committee reporting operational details.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group aligns telemetry protocols and develops open standards for multi-agent observability, agent execution context, and reasoning traces across the AAIF ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Focus Groups and Activities
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across specialized focus groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:
- **LLM Primitives**: Develops landscape surveys and gap analyses combining model context protocol audits and primitive evaluation frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates agent state management, persistence layers, and context reviews across industry implementations and academic research [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Evaluates telemetry and tracking mechanisms for complex multi-agent execution graphs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Explores telemetry for step-by-step reasoning, memory systems, and white-box tracing integration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy**: Refines and contributes core telemetry terms to the cross-WG [Taxonomy specification](../specification/taxonomy.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-25**: Working group repository made public, issue trackers established for focus groups, and monthly Technical Committee reporting cadences adopted [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices for accurate and reliable enterprise AI agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing the standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group was formally approved on May 15, 2026[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Focus Areas

The working group focuses on classifying failure modes in agentic systems, defining resilience mechanisms, and establishing shared recommendations for proactive and reactive failure mitigation[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### In Scope
- **Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks**: Defining the dimensions, failure modes, evaluation techniques, and quality thresholds for agent performance standards[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Standardizing proactive structural requirements, including verification loops and grounding to authoritative data sources (trust anchors)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Specifying safe-state restoration, rollback mechanisms, automated compensatory actions, and human-in-the-loop escalation triggers[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### Out of Scope
- Foundation model internals, pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- Log and trace emission mechanics, which are delegated to the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- Developing production runtimes, commercial guardrail platforms, or regulatory compliance frameworks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Deliverables

The group organizes its work across a canonical deliverable framework (D1–D6) alongside internal tracking assets[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Taxonomy & Architectural Framing)**: Architectural frame for accuracy and reliability terminology, covering evaluation subjects, output quality, grounding, failure root causes, and correction mechanisms[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey)**: Applied B2B enterprise evidence report evaluating multi-persona operational requirements, benchmark landscapes, and tooling/interoperability gaps[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15**: Working Group charter formally approved[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **2026-06-29**: Submitted first monthly report detailing execution on D1 vocabulary framing, D2 gap analysis, and cross-working group liaisons[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Taxonomy
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working group vocabulary and classification framework establishing unified terms and conceptual boundaries across AAIF domains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Taxonomy is a cross-working group foundation initiative establishing a shared vocabulary, conceptual boundaries, and unified classification system across all Agentic AI Foundation domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]. It coordinates cross-domain terminology from working groups such as [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Term Harmonization and Governance

The workstream operates an asynchronous, cross-group terminology reconciliation pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]:
- **Working Group Delegates**: Each working group appoints designated liaisons to contribute domain-specific vocabularies and reconcile cross-cutting definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **Unified Term Registry**: Universal terms spanning multiple domains—such as core definitions of agents, agency boundaries, and human curation—are evaluated in a shared tracking registry[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Review Schema**: Terms are tracked alongside structured definitions, citations, conflicting usage analyses, and working group ownership metadata[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-22**: Taxonomy and Landscape workstream aligned on delegate roles, established offline reconciliation workflows for universal terms, and initiated boundary definition for autonomous agents[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

mutations.rationale: Multiple meeting notes confirm the existence, mission, structure, and activities of the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream, which is nearing charter approval.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group responsible for establishing a shared taxonomy standard and maintaining the ecosystem directory using CNCF-style metadata.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS-Taxonomy & Landscape) is responsible for developing a unified, cross-working group vocabulary (taxonomy) and maintaining a high-level directory of the Agentic AI ecosystem (landscape) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Its primary goals are to eliminate siloed terminology and prevent duplicate research across the foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. The workstream reports monthly to the Technical Committee (TC) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream utilizes a PR-driven, asynchronous workflow for all contributions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
*   **Taxonomy:** Definitions are structured to include both a quick summary and a comprehensive description field to resolve ambiguity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. The workstream aligned on using a CNCF-style metadata structure for the shared vocabulary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Definitions are actively aligned with international standards such as ISO and NIST [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
*   **Landscape:** The ecosystem directory utilizes a CNCF-style structure and is integrated with the existing `landscape.aif.io` project [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Governance and Process
A core team consisting of active delegates from each working group drives the taxonomy curation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]. Terminology conflicts are resolved through a formal review process requiring approval from designated domain editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. The workstream mandates human oversight for definition creation and is developing an [AI Usage Policy](../governance/ai-usage-policy.md) and a style guide for consistency [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

The workstream follows specific style guidance for all communication, emphasizing a neutral, direct, and professional voice, using complete thoughts, and avoiding contrastive language [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

mutations.rationale: The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream has defined the specific metadata schema (CNCF-style) and required structure (summary + description) for the cross-working group vocabulary.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Working Group Taxonomy
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working group vocabulary and classification framework establishing unified terms and conceptual boundaries using a CNCF-style metadata structure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Working Group Taxonomy is the unified vocabulary standard designed to eliminate siloed terminology and prevent duplicate research across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). It is managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Specification
The taxonomy utilizes a metadata structure based on the CNCF landscape tool format [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]. Each definition must include both a concise summary (catering to beginners) and a comprehensive description field (providing detailed scope notes for experts) to resolve ambiguity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Governance
All contributions are managed via a PR-driven, asynchronous workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Terminology conflicts are resolved by designated domain editors, typically delegates from the relevant working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. The workstream actively seeks alignment with established international standards such as ISO and NIST [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

mutations.rationale: The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream confirmed that the landscape initiative will adopt the CNCF-style structure and integrate with the existing landscape.aif.io project.

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an ecosystem directory maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). It catalogs open source software, open standards, and member projects relevant to the Agentic AI domain [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

# Specification
The landscape utilizes a structure based on the CNCF landscape tool format [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985]. The data structure distinguishes between member-driven and external entities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Implementation
The landscape map efforts are integrated with the existing `landscape.aif.io` project [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

proposed_concept.description: Policy mandating human oversight and judgment when utilizing AI tools for generating or reviewing technical definitions and documentation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AI Usage Policy is being developed to ensure quality and consistency across foundation documentation, particularly within the [Cross-Working Group Taxonomy](../specification/taxonomy.md). It mandates human oversight and judgment when utilizing AI tools for generating or reviewing content [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

# Scope
This policy is intended to govern the use of AI in drafting definitions and related documentation, ensuring that human domain editors maintain final authority and responsibility for accuracy and alignment with standards [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
