proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is responsible for establishing a unified conceptual framework, SKOS-Lite data schemas, and the interactive ecosystem landscape for the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1] The group is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains core specifications and operational tooling across two main tracks:
- **Taxonomy Framework**: Standardized via a SKOS-Lite data schema to structure cross-domain terminology contributed by delegates across AAIF working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Built using a CNCF-style configuration format and published via a continuous integration portal pipeline to catalog open source projects, standards, and member technologies.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Approved workstream charter across participating working groups, onboarded formal WG delegates, established a unified terminology review spreadsheet, and defined SKOS-Lite and CNCF-style data schemas.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# References

- [Agentic AI Landscape](../initiatives/agentic-ai-landscape.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) aligns agentic AI technical implementations with global regulatory frameworks, compliance requirements, and risk mitigation practices.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454] The group is co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group produces landscape assessments, risk benchmarks, and regulatory gap analyses:
- **Policy Framework Mapping**: Cataloging and comparative analysis of existing global AI policy guidance, standards, and statutory requirements.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]
- **Gap and Comparative Analysis**: Structured sprints identifying discrepancies between prevailing regulatory baselines and practical agent deployment architectures.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Completed a 3-month landscape assessment mapping existing agentic AI policy frameworks and standards, and initiated a follow-on 3-month gap analysis sprint.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# References
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Working Group Lifecycle](../governance/working-group-lifecycle.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning telemetry protocols and developing standards for multi-agent observability and distributed tracing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group establishes standards, telemetry protocols, and data models for monitoring, tracing, and debugging autonomous and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] The working group is co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical initiatives and focus groups cover:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Instrumentation standards and telemetry interfaces for model invocations and communication protocols.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Telemetry and trace models for multi-agent orchestration, coordination, and distributed execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **Agentic State, Context & Reasoning**: Models capturing runtime context transitions, state evolution, and step-level decision paths.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]
- **Use Cases and Gap Analysis**: Detailed mapping of observability architectural gaps across agentic frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Finalized 6-month deliverables charter, launched initial focus groups, drafted use case and gap analysis documents, and contributed terminology to the Taxonomy workstream.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **July 2026**: Initiated consolidation of overlapping focus groups (merging LLM Primitives with Protocol Observability) and reviewed external discovery interfaces including Agentic Resource Discovery.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]

# References
- [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-WG security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPWG) defines reference architectures, threat models, security best practices, and evaluation criteria to secure autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems across enterprise and open-source deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group conducts its technical scope through several key workstreams and deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, this effort conducts gap analysis across eight identified security domains, integrating MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF).
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security guidance and operational recommendations for building and deploying agent workflows.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, establishing reusable security patterns and architectural templates.
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing a standardized security review mechanism across all AAIF working groups.

# Lifecycle History

- **External Alignment & Standards**: SPWG collaborates and aligns with broader industry standards and external initiatives, including OWASP AI Top 10, AARM, ETSI TC SAI, and Linux Foundation FINOS AI initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-WG Integration**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as SPWG delegates to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize security-specific terminology [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group responsible for establishing a shared taxonomy standard and maintaining the ecosystem landscape directory.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream establishes unified terminology, concept boundaries, and classification taxonomies across all AAIF working groups while curating an interactive landscape of the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates an asynchronous and cross-group review process [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]:

- **Unified Review Workflow**: Delegates from each AAIF working group contribute 10–20 core domain terms toward an initial v1.0 release.
- **Term Harmonization & Consensus Tracking**: The group maintains a unified working sheet tracking over 250 candidate terms. Terms are evaluated for relevance, categorized into universal or domain-specific groupings, or marked with a consensus-driven "cull" status to filter generic non-agent concepts.
- **Cross-Group Coordination**: Contentious or overlapping terms (such as "agent" vs. "bot", "identity", and "Agent Card") are coordinated with relevant working groups and surfaced via shared communication channels before finalizing definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026**: Transitioned charter to formal operations, instituting weekly syncs and initial raw-term intake [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **July 2026**: Began formal execution and review phase on unified taxonomy sheet, establishing instructions guidelines, consensus columns, and extending meeting times to support term debates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

mutations.rationale: Update Security & Privacy WG with confirmed leadership, five active workstreams, taxonomy handoff, external alignment efforts, and reporting process.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, security best practices, architectural design patterns, and cross-ecosystem alignment for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Led by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group focuses on securing autonomous AI agent architectures, tool execution, and multi-agent interactions across enterprise environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates across five active workstreams covering threat modeling, best practices, and ecosystem harmonization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Developing structured threat assessment frameworks tailored to agentic workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Drafting actionable guidelines and hardening practices for deploying agent systems safely [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **Cross-WG Alignment**: Providing designated delegates to the foundation-wide [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
- **External Collaboration**: Coordinating alignment and shared messaging with external industry efforts including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History
- June 2026: Working group transitioned repositories to public, confirmed leads across all five workstreams, transferred taxonomy management to the cross-WG initiative, and published its first monthly report to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].
- Reporting Cadence: Submits monthly progress updates to the Technical Committee by the last business day of each month under a 7-day review window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream curates and maintains a shared glossary of agentic AI terms and a foundation-wide ecosystem landscape for the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and co-chaired by Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream acts as a horizontal harmonization body to ensure all working groups align on consistent terminology and a unified view of the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates on a federated curation model utilizing nominated Domain Editors (delegates) from across AAIF vertical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]:

- **SKOS-Lite Vocabulary Standard**: Curates core vocabulary terms using a lightweight schema supporting `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **CNCF-Style Landscape Map**: Maintains an interactive catalog (`landscape.yml`) whose categorization categories evolve iteratively via delegate consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Cross-WG Arbitration**: Ingests and consolidates domain glossaries to eliminate siloed definitions and redundant ecosystem surveys [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Automated Web Publishing**: Continuous deployment workflows build and publish the Shared Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape Map directly to GitHub Pages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-06-21: Charter formally approved, setting up weekly delegate synchronization, federated glossaries ingestion, and automated deployment pipelines [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Overview

The working group operates under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) alongside peer technical working groups in the foundation.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

# Leadership and Governance

The working group chairs are appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the working group.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

- **Co-Chair:** Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Current Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and security review frameworks for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical output across five primary deliverables and workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing baseline threat models and framework designs for agent architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, documenting practical security engineering guidelines for agent implementations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, categorizing reusable architectural security and privacy design patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, developing review criteria to assess security across other AAIF technical outputs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration:** Security delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman coordinate with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define security-specific concepts (such as sessions, constraints, and guardrails) within the unified [Taxonomy](../specification/taxonomy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# External Collaborations

The working group coordinates with external security organizations, including unofficial collaboration with OWASP while formal relationships are reviewed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow models, execution semantics, and integration patterns for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, developing open specifications, interoperability guidelines, and design patterns that enable agent workflows to operate across diverse frameworks, tools, and execution environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Scope

The working group's charter covers three core areas:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Defining standard primitives (such as tasks, tool calls, branching, and sub-agents), representation formats, execution semantics (step ordering, parallelism, conditional branching), and handoff semantics between agents and sub-agents.
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution**: Formulating patterns for multi-step workflows spanning minutes to days, including state persistence models, partial completion resumption, retries, idempotency, failure recovery, and workflow-level audit logs (distinct from runtime telemetry handled by [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)).
- **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination**: Specifying standard workflow patterns for interacting with external systems, APIs, CLIs, services, and human-in-the-loop reviewers.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-13**: Charter approved under the leadership of Chair Yaron Schneider and Co-Chair Adam Seligman.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **2026-07-23**: Charter updated to clarify scope and execution semantics.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) focuses on developing open standards, evaluation methodologies, and practical benchmarks for assessing accuracy, consistency, robustness, and operational reliability in agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Key Deliverables and Initiatives

- **D1 (Terminology and Methodology)**: A supporting deliverable providing academic and literature grounding for agent reliability. Terminology execution is structured into three milestones; Milestone 1 covers 41 terms structured around outcome correctness, consistency across runs, perturbation robustness, and operational system reliability.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e] Initial terms feed into the shared [Taxonomy](../specification/taxonomy.md) effort.
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis)**: An initiative analyzing practitioner pain points, requirements, and gaps blocking enterprise adoption, transitioning from a pure benchmark inventory toward practitioner-grounded evaluation frameworks.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Cross-WG Liaisons**: Active coordination with related working groups, including an initial liaison established with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Published report under Chairs Jordan Augé and Casper Nielsen detailing D1 PR drafting, terminology milestone batches, and D2 reframing toward practitioner priorities.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group identifying and promoting open standards and reference architectures for AI agent identity, delegation, attestation, and verifiable action records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group identifies and promotes open standards and architectural patterns for agent identity, authentication, delegation, dynamic authorization, attestation, and verifiable action records across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. The working group is chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across three active sub-working groups[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]:

- **Taxonomy Sub-WG:** Establishes shared definitions for terms including Agent, Action Record, Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop. It defines the *Action Record* as a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of a single consequential action—distinguishing verifiable evidence intended for auditors or counterparties from operational telemetry handled by [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Reference Architecture Sub-WG:** Develops a component model spanning Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation. It establishes the rule that sub-agents cannot hold more permissions than their delegating agent, which cannot exceed the initiating user's permissions[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Critical Use Cases Sub-WG:** Formulates functional requirements across Internal, B2B, and B2C interaction models, focusing on verifiable delegation, dynamic per-request authorization, content-private action records, and principal-attested revocation[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

The group profiles OAuth 2.0 as a candidate normative baseline for cross-platform agent authorization tokens, delegation chains, and scope expression while treating internal backend policy enforcement as autonomous[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026:** Advanced taxonomy definitions and reference architecture component tables; initiated technical evaluations of NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) / Open Delegation and Identity Standard (ODIS) and the OpenID Foundation's agentic identity whitepaper[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group mapping commerce capabilities, protocol interoperability, and fraud and trust signals across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group provides a protocol-neutral forum for cataloging, evaluating, and harmonizing open specifications, reference architectures, and interfaces across the agentic commerce lifecycle[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group focuses on commerce-facing interfaces and signals rather than merchant or platform backend internals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its core deliverable, the **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**, and companion gap analyses across five core areas[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]:

- **Product Discovery:** Delineates asynchronous catalog/product feeds from live merchant and marketplace querying, analyzing source discovery, data normalization, freshness, and trust[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Checkout & Negotiation:** Analyzes stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiations across protocols such as ACP and UCP, addressing extension mechanisms, transport bindings, and human-handoff flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Payment & Machine Execution:** Models payment capabilities through reusable handler, instrument, and credential abstractions, evaluating composition with specialized protocols such as the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Post-Purchase & Lifecycle Management:** Investigates order tracking, cancellations, refunds, returns, and dispute flows, distinguishing read-only observation from authorized state transitions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **Fraud & Trust Signals:** Differentiates agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk, developing models for verifiable intent, portable baseline signal exchange, and risk-triggered context step-ups across boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

Cross-cutting dependencies link to [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History
- **March 2026:** Initiated problem inventory and lifecycle-based landscape methodology[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **April 2026:** Formulated draft charter and analyzed discovery and checkout models across ACP and UCP[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026:** Approved charter and advanced payment handler abstractions and MPP protocol comparisons[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **June 2026:** Evaluated fraud signal boundaries, transaction evidence binding, and post-purchase lifecycle scopes[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group maps commerce capabilities, protocol interoperability, transaction execution, and trust mechanisms across autonomous agent transactions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26] Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses challenges including protocol fragmentation, merchant integration burden, delegated authority, and dispute resolution.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group evaluates candidate protocols and frameworks across the complete commerce lifecycle:
- **Capability Mapping**: Defining structured commerce lifecycles spanning discovery, eligibility checks, checkout, payment execution, and post-purchase state mutations such as cancellations, returns, refunds, and adjustments.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Protocol & Mandate Analysis**: Evaluating input protocols including Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), and x402 payment responses.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Agent Wallets & Authority**: Analyzing how bounded intents, payment mandates, and credential capabilities integrate into transactions without requiring complete commerce system reimplementation by merchants.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]

# Lifecycle History
- **February 2026**: Working group launched under co-chairs Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, compiling an actor and capability inventory spanning consumers, agents, merchants, wallets, payment providers, and banks.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]
- **July 2026**: Advanced post-purchase workflow analysis using UCP policy structures and explored agent wallet integration models with AP2 payment mandates.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]

# References
- Working Group Governance: [Working Group Lifecycle](../governance/working-group-lifecycle.md)
- Foundation Taxonomy: [Taxonomy](../specification/taxonomy.md)

# Overview
The AAIF Reference Architecture Skill (`aaif-ref-arch`) is an [Agent Skill](../specification/agent-skill.md) maintained within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) designed to produce standardized architecture evaluations for open-source AI agent tools, frameworks, and specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-22]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill automates a structured evaluation workflow:
- **Source Material Ingestion**: Analyzes target repository documentation, data models, schema definitions, APIs, runtime behavior, and reference implementations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]
- **Assessment Generation**: Produces a standardized markdown assessment covering objective, zoom level (primitive, orchestration, or system layer), pinned prerequisites, component architecture diagrams, telemetry instrumentation walkthroughs, sample trace outputs, cost profiles, and validation criteria.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]
- **Runtime Requirements**: Configured for the `kiro` runtime and requires internet access for git and GitHub repository content retrieval.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #22**: Merged initial `aaif-ref-arch` skill definition under the tracing landscape project to support technology investigation workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-22]

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: A methodology organizing reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs and required guarantees, rather than agent count topology.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Job-Oriented Architecture Model organizes reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs, guarantees, and exit states, rather than structural properties like agent count (single-agent vs. multi-agent) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. This approach ensures that architectures communicate scope and operational purpose clearly, aligning with how practitioners approach operational needs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

A **Reference Architecture** is defined as a complete composition of reusable patterns, required capabilities, boundaries, and guarantees for a specific job. A **Pattern** is an independently adoptable solution to one recurring workflow problem, retaining its own invariants and failure modes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. Architectures compose patterns, separating reusable components from complete compositions.

# Specification

Under this model, agent count (single-agent or multi-agent) remains a visible characteristic but is not the primary top-level taxonomy. The model requires that architectures are reviewed based on a recognizable job, explicit guarantees, and a clear composition of reusable patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

For example, the "single-agent process with human approval" is defined by its job: allowing an agent to propose an action while ensuring a human authorizes the exact action before the protected effect occurs. This is distinct from a policy-authorized operation, which would require a separate architecture due to different risk and attribution topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Pattern
proposed_concept.description: An independently adoptable solution to a recurring workflow sub-problem, defined by its invariants, failure modes, and implementation approaches.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

A Workflow Pattern is an independently adoptable solution addressing a recurring sub-problem within agentic workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. Patterns are context-free, focusing on the shape of the solution rather than specific deployment stories, product names, or use-case specifics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054]. Reference architectures compose multiple patterns.

# Specification

A pattern document must define the problem it solves, why that problem is difficult, and the abstract solution shape (ideally 2–4 boxes). Key components of a pattern specification include:

1.  **Invariants**: Properties that any implementation must guarantee, written such that they hold regardless of the specific product or mechanism used.
2.  **Failure Modes**: Concrete descriptions of what breaks if the invariants are violated.
3.  **Implementation Approaches**: Illustrative examples of documented mechanisms, distinguishing what the runtime provides versus what the implementation must add to satisfy the invariants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

Patterns may also document known uses outside of agentic AI to demonstrate that the shape is discovered, not invented, and to highlight the delta introduced by agentic workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

mutations.rationale: The WG adopted a template for documenting architectural decisions, including context, rationale, consequences, and alternatives considered.

proposed_concept.title: Architectural Decision Record (ADR)
proposed_concept.description: A structured document template used to record the context, decision, rationale, consequences, and alternatives considered for architectural choices.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Architectural Decision Record (ADR) template is used to document significant architectural choices made by the working group. It ensures transparency and provides historical context for why a particular path was chosen over alternatives [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407].

# Specification

An ADR must capture:

1.  **Context**: What prompted the decision, including the prior state and the ambiguity or constraint requiring resolution.
2.  **Decision**: The resolution itself.
3.  **Rationale**: The reasoning behind the decision.
4.  **Consequences**: What changes if the decision is adopted, including follow-on work and known tradeoffs.
5.  **Alternatives Considered**: The credible alternatives and why they were not selected [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407].

Decisions are tracked by status (Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Superseded) and include links to relevant review discussions or pull requests.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: A workflow pattern ensuring a named human must explicitly approve or reject an immutable proposal before a protected effect can occur.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern addresses the need for human judgment and accountability before a workflow executes an action with high risk, audit obligations, or ownership requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. It is used in architectures such as the single-agent process with human approval.

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern requires presenting an immutable proposal to a uniquely identified, authorized human principal. The workflow enters a durable wait state until an explicit decision (approve or reject) is recorded, bound to that specific proposal version. Timeout and escalation paths must be explicit outcomes, never resulting in implicit approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

## Invariants

Key invariants that must hold in any implementation include:

*   The approver must be a uniquely identified human principal authorized for the decision class; shared approval identities are prohibited.
*   The interaction surface must display the exact, immutable proposal version.
*   Approval and rejection must be explicit decisions; silence, timeout, or system error never constitute approval.
*   The decision record must capture the proposal version, approver identity, decision, and timestamp under the same run identity.
*   A changed proposal requires a new approval decision.
*   Pending approval has a deadline and a defined expiry or escalation path.
*   Duplicate, late, or conflicting decision events cannot resume or execute the run more than once [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

## Related Patterns

This pattern is related to the Proposal/Execution Split and Durable Wait patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes standardized telemetry models, trace context propagation mechanisms, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents and distributed multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7] Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group coordinates with OpenTelemetry and external standards bodies like the IETF/IRTF on agent telemetry formats and runtime accountability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into three consolidated focus tracks:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Focuses on observing Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), modeling skills as first-class observable entities, and analyzing cross-boundary observability gaps.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination)**: Develops telemetry specifications across peer-to-peer and application layers, including the Agent Behavior Trace Model proposal and context intelligence graph runtime prototypes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Agentic State & Context**: Develops combined reasoning and state observability approaches, including composable trust blueprints linking Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

The group collaborates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Work Stream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to maintain cross-foundation terminology alignment.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Design Specification
proposed_concept.description: A proposed machine-readable specification format and design method capturing agentic workflow designs across deterministic, model-assisted, and agent-driven systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflow Design Specification (WDS) is a proposed formal, machine-readable artifact within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that captures recommended agentic workflow designs for automated implementation by coding agents or human engineers.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21] It is paired with the Workflow Design Method (WDM), a repeatable procedure for translating business use cases into compliant workflow specifications.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification-driven architecture is structured around three core principles:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]

- **Spectrum-Wide Coverage**: Unifies deterministic, model-assisted, and agent-driven workflows under a single vocabulary, recommending the least-agentic pattern required for a given task rather than treating agent count as the core organizing factor.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]
- **Shared Design Artifact (WDS)**: Provides a standardized, machine-interpretable blueprint used as the direct input for downstream workflow synthesis and execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]
- **Workflow Design Method (WDM)**: Defines repeatable analysis steps executed by either human architects or AI agents to generate valid WDS blueprints from domain requirements.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG) advances the AAIF mission by establishing a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems. It extends open specifications and projects, producing interoperability guidelines and design patterns that allow agent workflows to operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Leadership and Operations

The current Chairs are Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato). They were appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the working group, with a term running from March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

The WG meets biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Workstreams

This WG maintains a dedicated workstream for establishing a shared vocabulary:

proposed_concept.description: A draft guide covering security domains like secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

This guide is a draft deliverable from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md). It aims to provide builders with both the rationale ("why") and implementation details ("what") for securing agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

The structure follows a failure-pattern / control / decision-framework approach [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Scope

The guide covers five primary security domains:
1.  Secrets management
2.  Secure tool invocation (including supply chain considerations)
3.  Guardrails
4.  Evaluation frameworks
5.  Post-incident forensics

# Exclusions

The guide explicitly excludes topics related to identity and delegated authorization architecture (such as SPIFFE/SVID or RFC 8693), as these topics are handled by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish a shared understanding of agent observability, aligning existing telemetry efforts, identifying gaps, and developing guidance and specifications for cross-framework interoperability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]. proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group produces open threat models, security best practices, design pattern catalogs, cross-working group review checklists, and security-focused contributions to the unified taxonomy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) for the term running March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The group holds biweekly public meetings on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

Active deliverables and workstreams include[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]:
- **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design](../deliverable/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)** (Alon Mazor, Fernando Lucktemberg): Evaluates agent security gaps across MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, with STRIDE and PASTA framework alignment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../deliverable/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md)** (Fernando Lucktemberg, Matthew Khouzam): Establishes implementation guidance and controls covering agent lifecycle, secrets management, and runtime security[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog** (Dan Kommatas, Sagar Dashora): Outlines reusable architectural patterns addressing agentic security and privacy constraints[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist** (Govindaraj Palanisamy): Provides horizontal security assessment criteria across peer working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape** (cross-WG delegates Jay White, Katherine Druckman): Aligns domain terminology with the cross-working group taxonomy effort[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-14**: Charter and initial deliverables approved unanimously by working group vote[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-05-26**: Charter formally ratified following Technical Committee review[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-07-31**: Initial pull requests published for the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and the Best Practices Guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **2026-08-04**: Clarified PR review process permitting working group merges within charter scope without waiting for TC approval, and designated all past meeting recordings and notes as public by default[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a deliverable developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to provide technical recommendations, guardrail patterns, and operational safeguards for agentic AI architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an AAIF deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) evaluating existing threat modeling methodologies against unique agentic AI threat vectors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream is led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The deliverable synthesizes threat landscape data across eight core areas by benchmarking against established security frameworks:
- MITRE ATLAS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- OWASP agentic AI security and governance publications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- MAESTRO framework[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

The workstream also investigates the adaptation of classical threat modeling methodologies, such as STRIDE and PASTA, to autonomous agent architectures, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool invocation surfaces, and human-user-agent interaction interfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-31**: Initial gap review draft published as PR #8 on the working group repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **2026-08-04**: Working group reviewed feedback incorporating STRIDE/PASTA mapping, UI/HUA considerations, and recent MCP security developments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance framework defining the proposal process, lifecycle stages (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review criteria for AAIF open technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Lifecycle Policy establishes the intake requirements, review criteria, and formal stages for technical projects hosted within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Managed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), it governs both external open-source projects seeking AAIF adoption and new initiatives formed directly within the foundation.

# Specification

## Proposal Process

Projects are submitted through the AAIF project proposals repository. Proposals require defined metadata, including project description, mission alignment, Technical Committee sponsorship, OSI-approved permissive licensing, release automation mechanics, public issue tracking, maintainer leadership structures, and documented governance practices[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Lifecycle Stages

Projects progress through four distinct stages based on maturity, governance, and ecosystem adoption[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:

- **Sandbox Stage**: Early-stage entry point for experimental or nascent projects aligning with AAIF scope.
- **Growth Stage**: Maturing projects demonstrating sustained adoption, active maintainer bases, and functional governance.
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade, high-impact projects serving as core infrastructure or standards for the agentic ecosystem.
- **Emeritus Stage**: Inactive or retired projects that have completed their lifecycle and transition out of active maintenance.

# Lifecycle History

Evaluations and stage promotions are conducted via an Annual Review Process supervised by the Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: A security design pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing in confidential computing environments while keeping agent execution outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Attested Isolated Runtime is a design pattern developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) addressing threat models where the infrastructure operator sits within the untrusted boundary[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. The pattern moves the policy decision point and evidence signer into a hardware-isolated environment (such as a Trusted Execution Environment / TEE) and gates data release upon appraisal by an independent verifier.

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Invariants

The pattern requires four foundational elements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:

1. **External Agent Execution**: The core agent logic remains outside the hardware-isolated trust boundary, preventing attacker-influenced inputs from expanding the Trusted Computing Base (TCB).
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing keys are generated strictly inside the isolated runtime boundary and bound to evidence artifacts.
3. **Policy Measurement Sealing**: Operational policies are sealed to specific environmental measurements and released only upon valid appraisal.
4. **Per-Unit-of-Work Verifier Appraisal**: An independent verifier appraises cryptographically signed evidence for each discrete unit of execution.

## Hardware and Standards Alignment

The specification supports vendor-neutral implementation across AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0 architectures, alongside a software-only evaluation mode[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. It maps to RFC 9334 (RATS), RFC 9711 (COSE), RFC 8747, IETF SCITT, and SLSA provenance standards.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning telemetry protocols, trace context propagation, cross-surface identity resolution, and observability standards for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open frameworks, trace context propagation standards, and telemetry specifications required to monitor, debug, and audit distributed AI agent execution flows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-27].

# Specification

## Scope and Use Cases

The group maintains a standardized catalog of telemetry use cases covering operational cost tracking, outcome attribution, auditability, and cross-boundary diagnostics. Key focus areas include:

- **Identity and Ownership (Category I)**: Standardizing canonical cross-surface identity resolution (Use Case I1) to correlate an actor's agent activity across IDEs, CLIs, CI pipelines, and cloud runtimes back to an owning organization and initiator for accurate cost and risk accounting[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-27].
- **Distributed Trace Context Propagation**: Passing causal context and session identifiers across agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent boundaries.
- **Audit Trails**: Ensuring verifiability and tamper-resistance of agent decisions and execution steps.

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Agent Skill
proposed_concept.description: An agent skill that performs structured first-pass triage, severity classification, root-cause hypothesizing, and prompt-injection-safe evaluation of GitHub issues.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `issue-analysis` agent skill equips an agent to perform structured first-pass triage and root-cause analysis on filed GitHub issues for repository maintainers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Conforming to the standard [agent skill specification](../specification/agent-skill.md), it establishes guardrails for handling untrusted issue contents as data rather than instructions, inspects local codebase context in a read-only mode, and grounds severity assessments in historical review precedents [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill prescribes a structured four-stage evaluation workflow:

1. **Evidence Ingestion and Prompt Injection Defense:** Incoming issue text is treated strictly as data within nonce-delimited boundaries. If text attempts to issue directives or trigger unauthorized actions (such as mass notifications or prompt overrides) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60], the skill records suspicion flags and notes while isolating the technical merits for analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Codebase Grounding:** The agent reads local repository files to map referenced behaviors to concrete file paths (e.g., `src/queue/consumer.ts`) rather than abstract subsystems, operating in a strictly read-only manner without executing network requests or builds [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
3. **Precedent Consultation:** Hand-written reviews stored in `references/` provide domain context on severity classifications and known architectural failure modes, guiding the agent to reference historical cases only when genuinely relevant [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
4. **Standardized Output Drafting:** Results are formatted according to a defined markdown template detailing classification type, severity rationale, affected components, falsifiable root-cause hypotheses, suggested maintainer actions, and open clarification questions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

mutations.rationale: Captures the PyTorch Profiler reference architecture published under the Observability and Traceability working group tracing landscape.

proposed_concept.title: PyTorch Profiler Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture defining full execution path capture from Python tensor operations to GPU kernels using PyTorch Profiler and Chrome Trace JSON.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The PyTorch Profiler Reference Architecture defines mechanisms for capturing the complete execution path of tensor operations—from Python-level operation dispatch through the C++ ATen backend down to GPU kernel execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]. Maintained within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability), it establishes standard telemetry capture patterns across hardware accelerators.

The profile captures operator names, input shapes, data types, stack traces, GPU kernel launches, and memory allocations, producing standardized Chrome Trace Format JSON consumable by timeline visualization tools such as Perfetto, TensorBoard, and Holistic Trace Analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture specifies integration points across execution tiers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]:

- **Python User Code**: Scoped profiling contexts using `torch.profiler.profile` with step iteration boundaries to capture forward, backward, and optimizer execution.
- **ATen Dispatcher**: `RecordFunction` callbacks hooked at operation dispatch to record input shapes, dtypes, and call stacks.
- **Hardware Acceleration Layer**: Activity tracing bridging the bundled Kineto tracing library with NVIDIA CUDA (via CUPTI) and AMD ROCm (via roctracer) to measure kernel execution and memory allocations.
- **Trace Export**: Generation of Chrome Trace JSON and aggregated summary tables indexed by operator names and input shapes.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-25**: Documented as an authoritative tracing landscape reference architecture within the Observability and Traceability Working Group[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].

mutations.rationale: Captures the OpenTelemetry reference architecture assessing OTel collector pipelines and GenAI semantic conventions for agent infrastructure.

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture evaluating OpenTelemetry (OTel) pipelines and GenAI semantic conventions as telemetry substrate for AI agent infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture defines how traces, metrics, and logs are instrumented, collected, processed, and exported across AI agent infrastructure, LLM gateways, and tool-execution servers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it positions OpenTelemetry (OTel) as the vendor-neutral telemetry plumbing connecting AI workflows to downstream observability backends[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture spans the complete data pipeline from client SDK instrumentation to collector export[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:
- **Application Instrumentation**: AI agents, LLM gateways, and MCP servers instrument operations using OTel SDKs and standardized `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Wire Protocol**: Transmits telemetry over OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) via gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP/protobuf (port 4318)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **OTel Collector Pipeline**: Ingests signals via receivers, applies batching and processing, and routes standardized spans to target backends[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Trace Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture specifying line-level code attribution tracing for AI coding agents using the Agent Trace specification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Trace Reference Architecture specifies a local-first instrumentation mechanism for AI coding agents to emit line-level code attribution traces into version-controlled repositories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]. Developed under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it enables vendor-neutral verification of AI model contributions during automated file edits and tool executions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification operates within a single invocation session without requiring external collector backends[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]:
- **Hook Integration**: Hooks into IDE and agent runtime lifecycle events such as `afterFileEdit`, `afterTabFileEdit`, and `PostToolUse`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Local Persistence**: Records trace data as newline-delimited JSON (`.agent-trace/traces.jsonl`) bound to version control revisions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Attribution Metadata**: Captures contributor identities, active models, modified file ranges, and conversation session IDs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

proposed_concept.title: FTrace Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture evaluating Linux kernel FTrace function tracing and event recording via tracefs for low-overhead agent runtime host analysis.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The FTrace Reference Architecture documents the Linux kernel's built-in function tracing and event recording infrastructure via the `tracefs` virtual filesystem interface[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]. Assessed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it illustrates zero-overhead instrumentation when disabled and ubiquitous availability on Linux systems running agent workloads[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

# Architecture / Specification
The FTrace architecture relies on native Linux kernel mechanisms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]:
- **Dynamic Patching**: Functions compiled with `-mfentry` default to a 5-byte NOP instruction and are dynamically patched to `call ftrace_caller` at runtime using kernel breakpoints[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Core Tracers**: Implements function tracers, function graph tracers, tracepoint event listeners, and in-kernel histogram aggregations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Data Path**: Writes trace events to lock-free, per-CPU ring buffers exposed through `/sys/kernel/tracing/`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

mutations.rationale: Captures the comparative assessment of Linux kernel tracing technologies across AAIF evaluation dimensions.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison Assessment
proposed_concept.description: A comparative assessment evaluating LTTng, perf, and FTrace across observability dimensions for agentic host environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison Assessment provides an architectural evaluation of the three primary Linux tracing frameworks—LTTng, Linux perf, and FTrace—across core observability, security, and performance dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. Published by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it provides guidance on selecting tracing tools for lower-layer host and runtime observability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-41c8aea6][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

# Architecture / Specification
The assessment compares the technologies across several architectural axes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]:
- **FTrace**: Built-in, zero external dependencies, primary strength in kernel function flow and entry/exit graphs via `tracefs`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **perf**: Built-in kernel subsystem optimized for hardware Performance Monitoring Unit (PMU) counters and statistical sampling[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **LTTng**: External module system with per-CPU lock-free ring buffers outputting Common Trace Format (CTF), tailored for unified kernel and userspace tracing (LTTng-UST)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture detailing instrumentation mechanisms and debugging interfaces across Linux device drivers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture documents the layered observability mechanisms available across the Linux driver subsystem, spanning structured device logging, dynamic debug (`dyndbg`), `TRACE_EVENT()` tracepoints, bus-specific tracers, and `debugfs` interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. Part of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) landscape, it provides operational visibility into hardware accelerators, network devices, and host buses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-41c8aea6][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Architecture / Specification
Driver instrumentation is organized across layered facilities[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]:
- **Structured Logging**: `dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, and `dev_err` associate messages directly with driver devices[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Dynamic Debug**: Runtime call-site activation via `dynamic_debug/control` for zero-overhead inactive logging[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Driver Tracepoints**: Statically defined `TRACE_EVENT` macros providing structured binary tracing integrated with tracefs and external consumers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

mutations.rationale: Captures the newly merged reference architecture for NVIDIA Nsight profiling tools across GPU-accelerated AI workloads.

proposed_concept.title: NVIDIA Nsight Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture evaluating NVIDIA Nsight Systems timeline tracing and Nsight Compute per-kernel profiling across GPU-accelerated AI execution paths.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The NVIDIA Nsight reference architecture defines the evaluation of GPU profiling and tracing tools across CUDA-accelerated machine learning and AI agent infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]. It covers two complementary profilers built on the CUDA Profiling Tools Interface (CUPTI) and the NVIDIA Tools Extension (NVTX) annotation framework: Nsight Systems (`nsys`) for end-to-end timeline tracing and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) for per-kernel hardware counter analysis.

Nsight operates between higher-level AI frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and the underlying GPU hardware, capturing execution metrics from application layer dispatches down to kernel execution, memory transfers, and multi-GPU NCCL communication [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

# Architecture / Specification

The Nsight architecture consists of two primary operational paths for observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]:

- **Nsight Systems (Timeline Observability)**: Uses CUPTI activity and callback APIs combined with OS-level sampling to record unified timeline traces spanning CPU thread dispatches, CUDA runtime API calls, GPU kernel execution intervals, memory copies, and user-defined NVTX markers. Traces are emitted as SQLite databases or exported to Chrome trace JSON format.
- **Nsight Compute (Kernel Profiling)**: Intercepts individual GPU kernel launches using hardware performance monitor (PM) counters and kernel replay. It provides granular hardware utilization statistics, including Tensor Core activity, roofline model analysis, memory throughput, and Warp occupancy.

Integration with upstream AI frameworks builds upon the model evaluated in the [PyTorch Profiler Reference Architecture](../deliverable/pytorch-profiler-reference-architecture.md), linking software runtime events to hardware kernel invocations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

# Lifecycle History

Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) within the hardware accelerator tracing landscape workstream [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].
