proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Workflow Orchestration Patterns Comparison
proposed_concept.description: A comparative reference matrix evaluating agentic AI workflow orchestration patterns across complexity, agency levels, and enterprise operational considerations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Workflow Orchestration Patterns Comparison is a reference deliverable from the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`) synthesizing workflow patterns from AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Anthropic documentation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab]. The deliverable classifies patterns by agency level and implementation complexity to guide practitioners in choosing appropriate orchestration topologies[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].

# Architecture / Specification

The comparative catalog organizes recurring workflow patterns into complexity and agency tiers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab]:

- **Low Complexity & Minimal/Low Agency**: LLM-Augmented Workflow, Single-Agent ReAct, Routing/Triage, and Sequential Prompt Chaining.
- **Medium Complexity & Moderate Agency**: Sequential Multi-Agent Pipelines, Parallel Fan-out/Fan-in, Iterative Loops, and Review & Critique (Maker-Checker).
- **High/Very High Complexity & Autonomous Agency**: Coordinator/Orchestrator-Workers, Autonomous ReAct Loops, Hierarchical Task Decomposition, Multi-Agent Swarms/Roundtables, and Hybrid Plan & Solve engines.
- **Control and Governance Overlays**: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval gates (`../specification/human-approval-gate.md`) and deterministic custom logic integrations.

### Selection Guidance

The matrix outlines selection heuristics based on subtask determinism, debugging requirements, tool count, and multi-perspective consensus needs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: A catalog of reusable design patterns and anti-patterns addressing secure memory, execution isolation, authorization, and runtime intervention in agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an AAIF deliverable curated by the Security and Privacy Working Group providing reusable architecture and implementation patterns for secure, privacy-preserving agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e]. Each pattern is structured in a problem, context, solution, and trade-offs format, pairing recommendations with anti-patterns where applicable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog covers foundational security and privacy domains for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e]:
- **Hooks and Checkpointing:** Lifecycle state interception, validation, and rollback checkpoints.
- **Human-in-the-Loop Patterns:** Escalation gates and operator oversight models.
- **Privacy-Preserving Execution:** Zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs, Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), and encrypted vector database designs.
- **Blast Radius Containment:** Limiting the scope and potential damage of rogue or compromised agent actions.
- **Secure Memory and Lifecycle Management:** Retention, data deletion, and data sovereignty across short-term and persistent memory stores.
- **Agent Containment and Runtime Intervention:** Kill switches, transaction rollback, permission downgrades, and off-task execution detection.
- **Agent Authorization Models:** Fine-grained authorization, identity delegation, and privilege enforcement.

# Lifecycle History
- Workstream Leads: Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e].
- Contributors: Aditya Gidh (IBM), Aileen Schultz (TELUS), Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), Hsiao-Ying Lin (Huawei), Jonas Pfoh (Bluerock), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), Saquib Saifee (IBM), and Sohrab Farooq (TELUS) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-21].

proposed_concept.description: A guide establishing actionable security guidance, guardrails, secrets management, and forensics across agentic AI lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, high-level operational and architectural guidance for builders and operators of agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250]. While complementary design pattern catalogs detail how to implement specific components, this guide articulates recommended practices, guardrails, and external reference frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide focuses on core security practices across the agent lifecycle [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250]:
- **Secrets Management:** Credential isolation, ephemeral token handling, and runtime key protection.
- **Secure Tool Invocation:** Safe tool dispatch, schema validation, and boundary enforcement during agent action execution.
- **Guardrails:** Policy enforcement and input/output guardrails mitigating prompt injection and out-of-scope behaviors.
- **Evaluation Frameworks:** Standardized testing, red-teaming, and security evaluation methodology.
- **Post-Incident Forensics:** Telemetry retention, audit logs, and diagnostic paths for post-compromise investigation.
- **External Framework References:** Curated mappings and pointers to external security frameworks and standards.

# Lifecycle History
- Workstream Leads: Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250].
- Contributors: Aditya Gidh (IBM), Allie Howe (Keycard), Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Bar Kaduri (Capsule), Brad Tumy (Twilio), Dan Kommatas (Circle), Erin Farr (IBM), Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), Hsiao-Ying Lin (Huawei), Jonas Pfoh (Bluerock), Mitesh Bhawsar (Equinix), Mithil Patel (Equinix), Philipp Tiesel (SAP), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), Saquib Saifee (IBM), Sohrab Farooq (TELUS), and Tom Sheffler (Lenovo) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-21].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF working group dedicated to defining security controls, threat models, architectural patterns, and privacy frameworks for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output across multiple active workstreams:
- **Best Practices:** Produces the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../deliverable/agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md), led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), addressing secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, and forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-ea047250].
- **Design Patterns:** Produces the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../deliverable/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), curating architectural patterns for runtime containment, memory lifecycle, human-in-the-loop controls, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-6450bd6e].
- **Threat Modeling & Isolation:** Maintains threat modeling gap analyses and reference architectures including the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../deliverable/attested-isolated-runtime.md).

# Overview

The `aaif-create-online-series` skill provisions new AAIF online event series (such as reading groups, paper clubs, or webinars) under the top-level `Online/` Google Drive directory [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6]. It acts as the online counterpart to chapter creation, cloning the `TemplateSeries` folder and rebranding all contained assets for non-venue recurring programs [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].

# Architecture / Specification

The skill operates under strict tooling and file manipulation constraints [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6]:
- **Drive Execution Model**: All Google Drive reads, copies, and updates are executed via the `gws` CLI driven through Python [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6]. Desktop office suites like LibreOffice and `soffice` are prohibited to prevent font substitution and OOXML degradation [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].
- **Rebranding Rules**: Performs case-matched token replacement across document content and file names, substituting San Francisco template defaults with series names and Luma slugs (`aaif-<slug>`) [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].
- **Artifact Scaffolding**: Seeds an online-oriented `Event Tracker.docx` runbook (covering join links, streaming moderation, and recording workflows instead of venue logistics), `Attendee CRM.xlsx`, and presentation templates [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].

proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the intake, TC engagement bar, Q&A window, voting gates, and onboarding steps for incoming AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process defines the sequential operating procedure for reviewing, approving, and onboarding project submissions into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. It serves as the operational implementation of the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../governance/project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

The intake and approval pipeline runs primarily asynchronously across six sequential steps and supporting parallel milestones [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:

1. **Step 1 - Initial Intake**: The Foundation CTO, assisted by an automated intake agent performing technical compliance checks, screens submissions for completeness and alignment [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **Step 2 - TC Q&A Window**: An offline review window where proposals must satisfy a defined Technical Committee engagement bar [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. If engagement is unmet, an on-demand TC supporter mechanism is triggered [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Submissions may optionally present live if requested [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
3. **Parallel - Contributor Paperwork**: Contributor and IP legal paperwork runs in parallel with technical evaluation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
4. **Step 3 - TC Vote**: The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) votes asynchronously via LFX Vote on admission and initial lifecycle stage [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **Step 4 - GB Approval**: The Governing Board confirms organizational readiness and approves entry via LFX Vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **Step 5 - Legal Formation**: Linux Foundation Legal completes contribution agreements, charter formation, and asset transfers [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
7. **Step 6 - Technical Onboarding**: Linux Foundation IT and project submitters execute infrastructure transition and repository onboarding [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# References

- [`governance/technical-committee`](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [`governance/project-lifecycle-policy`](../governance/project-lifecycle-policy.md)

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: A workflow pattern deciding whether a candidate result may advance using explicit, repeatable checks rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Deterministic Acceptance Gate pattern evaluates a candidate result against explicit, reproducible criteria (such as test suites, contract checks, schema validation, or policy rules) and declared scope boundaries rather than relying on model self-assessment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. It provides verifiable evidence for a declared acceptance condition to determine if an activity result is permitted to advance to subsequent workflow steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

This pattern is a core building block in bounded agent workflows, such as bounded autonomous remediation, and complements iteration control patterns like [Bounded Convergence Loop](../specification/bounded-convergence-loop.md) and authorization splits like [Proposal/Execution Split](../specification/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658, ^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern evaluates both technical acceptance checks and task scope boundaries (target systems, allowed change class, accessed data, and permitted effects) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. Passing checks without satisfying scope limits does not constitute permission to proceed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

```text
Candidate result + declared scope
  │
  ▼
Run explicit checks and validate policy
  ├── [accepted and scope-valid] ──► Record acceptance evidence ──► Advance
  └── [not accepted / invalid]   ──► Return gate result to workflow control
```

## Invariants

1. **Pre-declared criteria:** Acceptance criteria and scope rules are defined before the candidate result is evaluated [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
2. **Evaluator independence:** The gate evaluation is independent of the model or agent that generated the candidate result [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
3. **Evidence binding:** Acceptance evidence is cryptographically or structurally bound to the exact candidate version or digest evaluated [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
4. **Fail closed:** A failed, missing, or ambiguous gate result never counts as acceptance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
5. **Bounded authority:** The gate's authority is restricted strictly to its declared contract; external or downstream effects require their own authorization controls [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

mutations.rationale: Captures the merged bounded convergence loop workflow pattern from the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: A workflow pattern safely iterating an agent-assisted task until a deterministic acceptance condition passes or ending in a defined non-success outcome.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Bounded Convergence Loop pattern governs iterative agent execution on a bounded task by pairing agent work with independent deterministic evaluation and strictly enforced retry budgets [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. It prevents open-ended execution, cost overruns, and self-certified completion by requiring an external gate and finite iteration, time, or cost limits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

This pattern is utilized in autonomous workflows such as bounded autonomous remediation and connects with [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../specification/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [Proposal/Execution Split](../specification/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0, ^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification

The workflow engine admits a single bounded task, exposes only the tools required for that scope, and evaluates candidate results through a deterministic gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. If the gate does not accept the result, retries are permitted only if declared retry budgets remain unexhausted [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

```text
Admit bounded task ──► Agent attempts permitted work
                             │
                             ▼
                   Deterministic gate evaluates result
                             ├── [accepted]     ──► Exit to controlled effect
                             └── [not accepted] ──► Configured retry criteria permit?
                                                      ├── [yes] ──► Agent retries
                                                      └── [no]  ──► Escalate, stop, or fail
```

## Invariants

1. **Pre-defined task boundary:** Scope, permitted tool capabilities, and acceptance criteria are set before the loop starts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
2. **Independent convergence decision:** An external deterministic gate evaluates all candidate results; the agent cannot declare its own success [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
3. **Mandatory budget bounds:** Every loop defines an iteration ceiling and at least one time or cost limit [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
4. **Audit and state durability:** The workflow records the attempt counter, evaluation outcomes, and exit reasons; restarts resume from recorded state without resetting budget limits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
5. **Scope enforcement:** Results that pass gate checks but breach declared scope are prohibited from executing protected effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

mutations.rationale: Captures the merged proposal/execution split workflow pattern from the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: A workflow pattern enforcing distinct roles and separate recording for proposal generation, authorization decisions, and effect execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal/Execution Split pattern separates intent generation, authorization, and effect execution across distinct architectural roles to enforce strict governance boundaries on probabilistic agents [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Under this pattern, an agent outputs immutable proposal data rather than triggering actions directly; an independent authorization authority reviews that exact proposal, and a dedicated workflow executor applies the effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

This pattern forms the baseline for high-risk, auditable operations and interfaces directly with patterns such as [Human Approval Gate](../specification/human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](../specification/durable-wait.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern enforces three decoupled roles and an auditable system of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:

```text
  proposer (agent)            authorization authority       executor (system)
        │                             │                            │
        ▼                             ▼                            ▼
   proposal ─────────► gate: authorize this exact ─ yes ─► workflow-controlled
   (immutable data,         proposal?                      execution of the
    not an action)            │                            authorized proposal
                              └─ no / invalid ──► terminal or     │
                                 recovery path                    ▼
                                                                effect
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    system of record: proposal · authority + decision evidence · effect
```

## Invariants

1. **Data over action:** The agent produces an immutable, structured proposal rather than invoking side-effecting tools [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
2. **Distinct authority:** Authorization is granted by an independent authority (human reviewer or versioned policy engine), never the proposing agent [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
3. **Exact authorization binding:** The execution step executes precisely the payload and parameters that were reviewed and authorized [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
4. **Inaccessible executor:** The execution mechanism and privileged credentials are inaccessible to the proposing agent [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
5. **Separate audit provenance:** Proposal content, authorization decisions, and final effect telemetry are logged as separate, correlated records in the system of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Intake Triage
proposed_concept.description: An agent skill for triaging community intake submissions across organizers, hosts, and speakers from the Intake Ops sheet.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-triage-intake` skill provides an operational review workflow to evaluate community intake submissions from the AAIF Community Intake Ops spreadsheet across organizers, event hosts, and speakers[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14]. It structures status tracking, deduplication logic, and candidate vetting before routing applicants to chapter onboarding or event programs[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].

# Architecture / Specification
## Status Lifecycle Model
Candidate rows progress through structured review states mapped to spreadsheet conditional formatting and CRM synchronization rules[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14]:
- `Prospect` / blank: Default initial state for unreviewed applicants (renamed from legacy `New` status)[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].
- `In progress`: Active preliminary review.
- `Tentative`: Candidate has passed initial profile vetting (e.g., LinkedIn verification) pending an interview or local champs introduction[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].
- `Interviewing`: Interview scheduled or in progress[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].
- `Accepted` / `Denied`: Terminal review decisions.
- `Inactive`: Inactive or non-responsive applicant.
- `Duplicate`: Parked repeat submission from an individual already in the queue[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].
- `Existing (from MLOps)`: Imported legacy organizer bypassing intermediate interview stages[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].

## Deduplication and Multi-Role Handling
A shared email address alone does not constitute a duplicate[^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14][^evt-community-events-pr-35]. The review flow distinguishes between identical resubmissions and legitimate multi-role applications (such as applying concurrently as an organizer and speaker) or multi-pitch submissions (such as distinct talk abstracts from a single speaker)[^evt-community-events-pr-35].

# References
- Specification: [agent-skill](../specification/agent-skill.md)
- Related skills: [aaif-clean-data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Capability Map
proposed_concept.description: A capability taxonomy and protocol mapping framework classifying agentic commerce transaction phases, signals, and evidence artifacts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Capability Map is a foundational deliverable from the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) defining structured capability rows, evidence artifacts, and protocol coverage across the agentic commerce lifecycle[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. It establishes a standardized framework for analyzing protocol interoperability and ecosystem gaps across purchasing, post-purchase resolution, and settlement[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification
## Post-Purchase Capability Dimensions
The post-purchase capability model categorizes lifecycle interactions into seven structured capability rows (P1–P7)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]:
- **P1: Eligibility Inquiry**: Validating return, refund, or warranty eligibility rules and conditions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P2: Remedy Offer and Negotiation**: Automated negotiation and selection of remedies including refunds, replacements, or store credit[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P3: Buyer Authorization and Consent Evidence**: Capturing explicit user approval and cryptographic consent for financial and return operations[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P4: State-Change Execution Signals**: Emitting and tracking fulfillment, return shipping, and carrier status updates[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P5: Evidence Binding**: Contextual and cryptographic binding of inspection reports, return proofs, and interaction history[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P6: Dispute and Claims Initiation**: Protocol-mediated dispute filing across payment and commerce rails[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **P7: Adjustment Ledger**: Reconciling ledgers, balance adjustments, and merchant-buyer settlements[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

## Evidence Contract and Protocol Mapping
Capabilities are mapped against emerging agentic commerce protocols including UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. For cross-boundary verification and auditability, the specification defines an 8-field bounded verdict envelope comprising `verdict`, `verifier`, `verifier_signature`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_fingerprints`, `verification_basis`, `witness_scope`, and `timestamp`[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# References
- Working Group: [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)
- Related Deliverable: [Agent Observability Use Cases](../deliverable/agent-observability-use-cases.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Pulse
proposed_concept.description: An agent skill for aggregating community updates across Slack, Drive, Sheets, and Luma to draft organizer update posts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-community-pulse` skill aggregates recent chapter activities, organizer milestones, calendar events, and repository changes to draft periodic "AAIF Community Organizer Update" announcements for community channels [^evt-community-events-pr-37]. Conforming to the [Agent Skill](../specification/agent-skill.md) specification, it assists operators by assembling dispersed community metrics into structured drafts without publishing autonomously [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates under a proposal-only human approval workflow [^evt-community-events-pr-37]:
- **Channel Ingestion**: Fetches recent discussions from `#local-champs` via read-only Slack API methods (`api.ok()`, `api.paged()`) with strict permission enforcement (`api.require_scopes`) [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Secure Caching**: Writes temporary cache files to a dedicated `0700` `.pulse-cache/` directory with `0600` file permissions using atomic file replacement (`tempfile.mkstemp` and `os.replace`), ensuring cache cleanup upon draft generation [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Operational Data Lookup**: Inspects the Chapters Drive folder and Intake Ops spreadsheets using Google Workspace (`gws`) tools to track onboarding organizers and active chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Event & Repository Monitoring**: Scans Luma calendars for upcoming events and inspects repository commit history (`git log`) to highlight tooling changes for organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History
The skill was introduced and merged in PR #37 of `aaif/community-events`, incorporating security hardening for path traversal prevention, atomic permissions, and robust Slack API pagination [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group aligning telemetry protocols, full-stack tracing, cross-surface identity, and behavior evaluation for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group surveys, coordinates, and standardizes agent observability across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1]. Its mandate covers telemetry protocols, hierarchical execution tracing, cross-agent identity propagation, and behavioral evaluation across heterogeneous agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group actively maintains a comprehensive survey of prior work and standard initiatives across the industry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1]:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions**: Standardized spans for agent lifecycles, workflow execution, tool execution, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions hosted in `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **Multi-Agent & Cross-Boundary Protocols**: Context propagation and distributed trace recomposition across agent boundaries, including AGNTCY Observe and A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol traceability extensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **Security & Identity Integration**: Semantic alignment with Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF 1.9) covering AI operations, agent identity attestation, and delegation tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **Runtime & Code Attribution**: Code attribution tracing via Agent Trace and trusted environment-derived signals via OpenTelemetry eBPF instrumentation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].

# Lifecycle History
The working group was formed under the AAIF at its launch in December 2025. In mid-2026, the working group updated its landscape survey to track dedicated OpenTelemetry GenAI repositories, multi-agent protocol integrations, and security schema alignments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-sync-badges
proposed_concept.description: An agent skill for generating and synchronizing AAIF chapter organizer badges across Google Drive folders.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync-badges` is an agent skill that automates generating and synchronizing AAIF chapter organizer badges in vector (SVG) and raster (PNG) formats directly to Google Drive [^evt-community-events-pr-38]. It reconciles the canonical list of community chapters against existing assets to upload only missing badges while enforcing idempotency [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill is organized into two primary script components [^evt-community-events-pr-38]:
1. **Badge Generator (`make_badges.py`)**: Generates ring and arc SVG badge designs and exports 1000px PNG renders using `cairosvg`, applying XML escaping to chapter display names to protect against markup injection [^evt-community-events-pr-38].
2. **Sync Engine (`sync_badges.py`)**: Uses Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) tooling to inspect chapter folders, diff them against badge targets, and upload missing badge artifacts with single-retry limits to avoid duplicate file creation [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

Execution is plan-only by default, supporting a `--write` flag to apply changes, `--regenerate` to trigger global badge asset refreshes, and `--chapter` to limit execution to a specific city [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History
Created in pull request #38 of `aaif/community-events` and validated against 89 active chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem. The WG produces open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns intended for adoption by providers, consumers, and peer working groups to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

# Deliverables
The WG is actively developing several key deliverables:
*   The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide, with the first version frozen and merged for internal socialization and public promotion [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
*   A catalog of reusable design patterns, including kill-switch patterns, with memory-related patterns planned [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
*   A code-facing deliverable converting security best practices into actionable static-analysis rules [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
*   Contributions to the unified AAIF taxonomy, targeting an initial version release by the end of September 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Leadership
The WG is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google). Their term runs from March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture for workflows where an agent prepares an action, a named human approves or rejects it, and a separate executor performs the protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This reference architecture defines a workflow pattern for ensuring human oversight before an agent triggers a protected effect (e.g., a refund, configuration change, or outbound message) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

The architecture guarantees that:
1.  No protected effect occurs without explicit human approval, and what executes is exactly what was approved.
2.  The run survives long waits (hours or days) required for approval, ensuring durability against restarts or crashes.
3.  Every run ends in a known state, with the full intent → decision → effect chain recorded in the audit log [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

# Architecture / Specification
This architecture is composed of three core workflow patterns:
*   [Proposal/execution split](../specification/proposal-execution-split.md)
*   [Human approval gate](../specification/human-approval-gate.md)
*   [Durable wait](../specification/durable-wait.md)

It requires capabilities including an execution engine, agent, tool access layer, state/context store, human interaction surface, workflow-controlled executor, and audit log [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

The design enforces a structural break between the agent's proposal generation and the protected effect execution. The agent constructs the proposal, but a separate, workflow-controlled executor acts only after explicit human approval is recorded [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Action Capsule is a data structure designed to serve as a middle layer between regulatory requirements and agent actions. It records what action was dispatched by the agent, what happened as a result, and whether the action was allowed to happen [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Specification
The capsule prevents tampering through the use of cryptographic proofs. It is designed to be verifiable, allowing the reconstruction of a complete execution trace from multiple capsules via a ledger system [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. The Observability and Traceability WG is exploring its integration with traceability efforts.

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: A reference architecture for workflows where an agent prepares an action, a named human approves or rejects the immutable proposal, and an execution engine applies it.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture is a reference architecture defined by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) for patterns where an AI agent proposes actions that require explicit human approval prior to execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

The pattern decouples generation, review, and execution into distinct runtime phases to ensure human accountability, auditable decision boundaries, and deterministic policy enforcement [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Invariants
1. **Proposal Immutability**: The agent compiles a candidate proposal payload (e.g., draft content, configuration change, pull request) that cannot be mutated once submitted for review [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
2. **Explicit Human Gate**: A named human operator must review and either approve or reject the immutable proposal via a [Human Approval Gate](../specification/human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
3. **Separated Execution**: Following approval, an automated execution engine or publisher applies the payload, enforcing a clean [Proposal-Execution Split](../specification/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

### Validated Use Cases
The architecture has been validated against standard content workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:
- **FAQ and Knowledge-Base Updates**: Agents draft additions or updates from tickets or discussions; subject-matter experts approve before publication [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Release Notes Drafting**: Agents summarize changelogs; release engineers review and authorize distribution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Listing Descriptions**: Marketing or catalog descriptions generated by agents are reviewed before being pushed live [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (also referred to as Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) serves as the bridge between global AI policy developments and the technical implementation of governance across agent systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Architecture / Specification

### Objectives & Methodology
- **Policy Instrument Landscape**: Analyzing global regulatory frameworks, best practices, standards, and legislative instruments applicable to agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Thematic Policy Mapping**: Mapping policy instruments against core governance themes to identify common regulatory requirements [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Gap Analysis**: Developing structured gap analyses comparing regulatory requirements against existing technical specifications and runtime implementations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Information Extraction Tooling**: Designing standardized AI prompts for structured, consistent extraction and synthesis of legal and standards texts [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group establishes open telemetry protocols, line-level tracing architectures, and cross-layer debugging specifications across agentic runtime environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

The group coordinates standard telemetry formats spanning low-level kernel tracing, GPU runtime events, and high-level agent action attribution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Group & External Liaisons
The working group maintains an intake tracker and liaison roster for coordination across standards bodies and external initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]:
- **External Standards Bodies**: OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Agent Trace, Monocle, and AGNTCY [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **Internal AAIF Touchpoints**: Technical Committee, sibling working groups (Security & Privacy, Workflows & Process Integration, Governance, Risk & Regulatory, Agentic Commerce), and the Taxonomy & Landscape workstream [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].
- **Inbound & Outbound Tracking**: Explicit tracking of issue flows and standardization requests across related initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate proposed 'Hard constraint' HITL pattern and 'Autonomy Graduation' lifecycle concepts from PR #42.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: A classification schema defining structural dimensions, autonomy graduation, and human-in-the-loop patterns across agentic AI use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema provides a standardized taxonomy and structural dimensional model for analyzing, classifying, and comparing agentic AI workloads and enterprise workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

## Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Patterns

The schema categorizes interaction models between human operators and autonomous agents [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]:

- **Approval Gate**: Checkpoints requiring human confirmation before advancing execution, typically utilized when confidence is low or systems are not yet fully trusted.
- **Exception Escalation**: Execution proceeds autonomously unless uncertainty, error thresholds, or unhandled conditions trigger human intervention.
- **None**: Fully autonomous execution without synchronous human intervention.
- **Hard Constraint**: Non-negotiable human accountability mandatory by law, regulation, or institutional policy (such as physician signatures, legal certifications, or board approvals) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. Unlike confidence-based approval gates, hard constraints do not relax as model capabilities or operational trust mature [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

## Autonomy Graduation

Workflows may evolve through an **Autonomy Graduation** lifecycle over time as operational reliability is proven [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]:

1. `Approval Gate` (initial deployment and supervised validation)
2. `Exception Escalation` (mature operations with intervention on boundary anomalies)
3. `None` (full autonomy)

Workflows bound by structural `Hard Constraint` requirements are explicitly excluded from graduating to lower oversight tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References

- Proposed by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-working group initiative maintaining unified agentic AI taxonomy vocabularies, landscape maps, and domain editor curation workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape workstream is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for maintaining a unified vocabulary, SKOS-Lite taxonomy schemas, and ecosystem landscape maps across all AAIF domain initiatives [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-58].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Domain Editors

Taxonomy management operates across multiple domain working groups through designated Domain Editors who represent their respective technical domains (such as Agentic Commerce, Security & Privacy, and Observability) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-58].

## Intake and Curation Lifecycle

Candidate concepts and terms follow a structured intake and review lifecycle [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-58]:

1. **Candidate Spreadsheet Intake**: Proposed terms and external definitions are aggregated in candidate intake sheets.
2. **Decision Flow**: Workstream participants evaluate candidate terms across three paths:
   - **Debate**: Ambiguous, overlapping, or contested terms requiring cross-WG alignment.
   - **Keep**: Terms accepted for formal integration into the shared taxonomy.
   - **Cull**: Out-of-scope, redundant, or deprecated terms removed from consideration.
3. **Socialization and Review**: Proposed additions are socialized with owning working groups before formal PR review and repository merge [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-58].

# References

- [Taxonomy Specification](../specification/taxonomy.md)
- [Agentic AI Landscape Initiative](../initiatives/agentic-ai-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Brand Foundation & Design System
proposed_concept.description: The visual design standards, token specifications, typography rules, and asset usage constraints governing AAIF documentation and reporting.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Foundation and Design System defines the visual principles, design tokens, typography, and asset usage rules for all official foundation publications, dashboards, and generated reports [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification

## Design System Rules

- **Primary Accent**: The primary action accent is black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve exclusively as internal accents within components [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Typography**: Single typeface family (Instrument Sans at weights 400, 500, 600, 700) across display and interface copy. Monospace fonts are restricted to metadata, eyebrows, and code [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Headings use weight 500 with tight tracking (`-0.02em`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Flat Aesthetic**: No drop shadows. Visual depth is established exclusively via 1px hairlines, inset strokes, and subtle paper tint steps (`--paper`, `--paper-2`, `--paper-3`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Dual Surfaces**: Designs utilize two first-class surfaces—white editorial and black plate. There is no automated `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Brand Asset and Logo Constraints

- **Mark Invariance**: The AAIF mark and logo SVGs must never be manually redrawn, approximated from memory, or altered beyond direct fill recoloring [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07, ^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Official Assets**:
  - `aaif-mark.svg`: Full mark and wordmark horizontal lockup [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07, ^evt-community-events-pr-41].
  - `aaif-mark-square.svg`: Mark alone for headers, avatars, and favicons [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
  - `aaif-logo-white.svg`: Full lockup formatted for black plate surfaces [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Agent Motif Restriction**: The primitive agent robot motif is permitted only for empty states, loading indicators, and event graphics; it is strictly prohibited on governance, board, or press deliverables [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# References

- [Blog Guidelines](./blog-guidelines.md)
- [Social Media Guidelines](./social-media-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: A workflow pattern deciding whether a candidate result may advance using explicit, repeatable checks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A workflow pattern deciding whether a candidate result may advance using explicit, repeatable checks.

The gate requires three properties to hold for every acceptance record, independent of the gate's required strength:
1. **Determinism of the verdict:** The decision (accept/reject) must be repeatable given the inputs.
2. **Binding of verdict to candidate:** The acceptance record must immutably link to the specific proposal or candidate result being evaluated.
3. **Preservation as execution evidence:** The acceptance record must be retained as part of the execution trace. [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]

# Architecture / Specification
The minimum evidence required for a deterministic gate to be considered strong enough scales with the potential impact of the permitted effect. This strength is tied to two properties of the effect: the *blast radius* (the scope of potential damage or unintended consequences) and the *reversal cost* (the effort or resources required to undo the effect). [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]

# References
- Related pattern: [Bounded Convergence Loop](../specification/bounded-convergence-loop.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent → Tool Boundary Deep-Dive: Local CLI Realization
proposed_concept.description: Analysis of the Agent → Tool semantic boundary and Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary, identifying observability gaps in local CLI execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This document analyzes the observability requirements and gaps across the **Agent → Tool Boundary**, specifically focusing on the realization where an agent invokes a tool via a local Command Line Interface (CLI) subprocess [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

The analysis distinguishes between two related boundaries:
1. **Agent → Tool semantic boundary:** Describes the agent-level decision, tool selection, and invocation.
2. **Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary:** Describes the operational mechanism of process launch, environment construction, and result observation.

# Architecture / Specification
The deep dive uses a matrix approach to evaluate observability across six dimensions for the local CLI realization: Identity, Context, Relationship, Lifecycle, Outcome, and Provenance.

Key gaps identified include:
*   **Identity:** Lack of a common cross-runtime identity binding the agent tool call, the exact executable artifact that ran, and the principal on whose behalf it ran. Executable digest and version are not consistently available.
*   **Context:** Inconsistent adoption of environment variable carriers for context propagation across process boundaries. Common context elements like turn/task identity, deadline, budget, and policy lack a common local-CLI profile.
*   **Outcome:** A successful exit code does not describe files, APIs, or resources changed. Side-effect manifests, partial results, and compensation outcomes are not standardized.

Context propagation must occur during process creation, as instrumentation based only on a transcript after the child exits is too late to establish stable causal context for the child process. [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]

# References
- Related Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group identifying and promoting open standards and reference architectures for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
AAIF working group identifying and promoting open standards and reference architectures for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) focuses on ensuring agents can be discovered, prove who they are, who they act for, what they are allowed to do, and what human approvals occurred, enabling secure, privacy-preserving, and auditable agent interactions across systems and organizational boundaries. [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

# Architecture / Specification
The work is organized into several breakout groups:
*   **Use Cases:** Grounds the work in enterprise and consumer scenarios and derives identity and trust requirements.
*   **Reference Architecture:** Describes the actors, components, trust relationships, and interoperability gaps needed to support agent identity and delegated authority.
*   **Taxonomy coordination:** Develops and socializes I&T terminology, coordinating with the cross-working-group Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream. [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]

# Lifecycle History
The current chairs are Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE), serving a term from March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027. [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

proposed_concept.title: Critical Use Cases Workstream
proposed_concept.description: A workstream within the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group cataloging and classifying production agentic workflows against verified production deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Critical Use Cases Workstream is an initiative within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../workflows-and-process-integration.md) tasked with identifying and cataloging reusable workflow patterns from real-world, production-deployed agentic applications[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]. Rather than serving as a subjective prioritization body, the workstream operates as an empirical classification and sourcing exercise[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains two central artifacts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:
- **Classification Schema (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`)**: A structured taxonomy defining structural execution dimensions, autonomy levels, and coordination patterns (see [Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema](../../deliverable/agentic-use-cases-classification-schema.md))[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].
- **Use Case Inventory (`use-case-inventory.md`)**: A comprehensive table mapping observed production workflows against schema dimensions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

### Evidentiary Standard
The workstream mandates strict citation criteria for inventory rows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:
- Every Notes entry must cite primary vendor product documentation, engineering blogs, or deployment announcements that confirm actual production usage rather than hypothetical capability[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].
- Requires at least one verified primary citation per use case, with three target citations per row[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].
- Dimensions lacking verified structural evidence must remain designated as `Unspecified: insufficient source detail`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Lifecycle History
- Workstream structure, evidentiary criteria, and inventory documentation proposed via PR#46[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

mutations.rationale: Update the classification schema deliverable with strict evidentiary standards and operational inventory criteria established by the workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: A classification schema and empirical inventory framework categorizing agentic workflow structures, execution patterns, and evidentiary standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema provides a structured framework for categorizing, analyzing, and benchmarking agentic workflows observed in real-world software deployments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]. Maintained by the [Critical Use Cases Workstream](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration/critical-use-cases-workstream.md), the deliverable links structural workflow dimensions with an empirical inventory of verified production systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification
The schema evaluates agentic systems across several core architectural dimensions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:

### Structural Dimensions
- **Execution Topology**: Structural flow of execution including sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out, and convergence loops[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Agent Coordination**: Classification of agent roles from single-agent setups to fixed/scripted orchestration and dynamic AI-coordinated planning supervisors[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Human Autonomy Boundaries**: Graduations of human oversight including notification-only, human-in-the-loop approval gates, and autonomous execution boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

### Evidentiary Standards
Classifications within the accompanying inventory (`use-case-inventory.md`) are constrained by explicit verification criteria[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:
- Classifications must cite primary vendor architectural blogs or technical product documentation evidencing runtime execution structure[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- Claims where public sources only describe high-level capabilities without detailing concurrency or coordination topology are strictly marked as `Unspecified: insufficient source detail` until verified[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
- Initial classification schema developed in the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group.
- Evidentiary standards and citation verification processes integrated via PR#39, PR#46, and PR#48[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Meta-Harness
proposed_concept.description: An execution harness or orchestration framework that manages, coordinates, or composes multiple underlying agent harnesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A meta-harness is an architectural layer and execution framework that coordinates, configures, or composes multiple distinct agent harnesses[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48]. While an individual harness wraps and manages the execution lifecycle of a single agent instance, a meta-harness operates at a higher tier of abstraction across multi-agent or multi-runtime topologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
Within the AAIF taxonomy schema, meta-harness relates directly to `taxonomy/harness` via compositional relationships rather than mutual exclusion[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48]:
- **Compositional Relationship**: A meta-harness encapsulates or supervises multiple child harnesses, managing context handoffs, credential boundaries, and joint task lifecycles[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].
- **Taxonomy Placement**: Linked bidirectionally with [Harness](../taxonomy/harness.md) through `relatedTerms`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History
- Defined and approved by the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream via PR #48, expanding upon foundational runtime terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

An execution environment and runtime wrapper managing agent lifecycle, tool execution, context injection, and policy boundary enforcement[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

A harness provides the direct boundary between an agent core and host operating systems, tools, or memory stores. In multi-agent configurations, individual harnesses may be composed and orchestrated under a [Meta-Harness](../taxonomy/meta-harness.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

The designation provides governance clarity across agentic pipelines by distinguishing automated synthesis from reviewed knowledge bases[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39]:
- **Assurance Signal**: Serves as a trust boundary indicator within agentic workflows and landscape taxonomies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Cases Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: A classification schema and empirical inventory framework categorizing agentic workflow structures, evidentiary standards, and deployment patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A classification schema and empirical inventory framework developed by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group to evaluate and categorize production agentic workflows across complexity tiers, coordination modes, and human oversight topologies[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework establishes explicit categorization dimensions and strict evidentiary thresholds for cataloging real-world deployments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Evidentiary Standard**: Requires vendor primary documentation or confirmed customer deployment announcements (excluding secondary blogs, analyst commentary, and unverified preprints) to maintain empirical rigor[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Classification Criteria**: Standardizes fields across coordination topology, human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns, approval gate subtypes, and single- vs multi-agent rationale[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Gaps and Mitigations**: Formally identifies source rot and documentation obsolescence within schema governance[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Lifecycle History
- Developed under the Critical Use Cases Workstream within [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

mutations.rationale: Add the agreed taxonomy definition and scope note for Human in the loop merged in ws-taxonomy-landscape PR #40.

proposed_concept.title: Human in the Loop
proposed_concept.description: An execution pattern requiring an explicit human approval or decision checkpoint before an agent action can proceed.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Human in the loop (HITL) is an interaction and oversight pattern in which an AI agent cannot proceed beyond specific execution checkpoints without explicit human authorization, review, or input [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification
HITL establishes synchronous verification boundaries within agent workflows, contrasting with autonomous execution or human-on-the-loop oversight where monitoring occurs post-action or asynchronously [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40]. In practice, it interfaces directly with approval mechanisms such as [human approval gates](../specification/human-approval-gate.md) and agent handoff protocols [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40].

mutations.rationale: Add the authoritative Identity & Trust definition for Delegation merged in ws-taxonomy-landscape PR #42.

proposed_concept.title: Delegation
proposed_concept.description: The transfer of authority, execution scope, or credentials from a principal to an agent or between collaborating agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Delegation is the process and mechanism of transferring authority, execution scope, or credentials from a principal (such as a human user or an orchestrating system) to an agent, or between collaborating agents [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification
In agentic architectures, delegation establishes the authorization boundaries and policy envelopes under which an agent executes tasks on behalf of another entity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]. Delegation is closely linked to task handoff mechanisms and [context propagation](../taxonomy/context-propagation.md) across multi-agent workflows [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].

mutations.rationale: Add the authoritative Identity & Trust definition for Attestation merged in ws-taxonomy-landscape PR #42.

proposed_concept.title: Attestation
proposed_concept.description: Cryptographic or verifiable proof establishing the state, identity, or execution integrity of an agent runtime or component.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Attestation is the mechanism of providing verifiable cryptographic evidence or assertions regarding the identity, software configuration, and execution integrity of an agent runtime or environment [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification
Attestation forms a core requirement for verifiable agentic systems, allowing external verifiers to authenticate that an agent is executing inside an untampered environment with expected policy constraints [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]. It directly supports patterns like [attested isolated runtimes](../deliverable/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and verifiable action records [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: The governing body responsible for reviewing project proposals, recommending projects, and setting technical standards across the foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), overseeing technical standards, project lifecycles, and foundation-wide architectural direction [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification
The TC manages project lifecycle intake, establishes working group guidelines, and evaluates projects advancing through Sandbox, Growth, and Impact stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

## Committee Membership
Founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for the term of March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Anthropic) - TC Chair
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Microsoft) - TC Co-Chair
- **Alan Blount** (Google)
- **Bradley Axen** (Block)
- **James Ward** (Amazon Web Services)
- **Nick Cooper** (OpenAI)
- **Sambhav Kothari** (Bloomberg)
- **Steve Faulkner** (Cloudflare)

## Foundation Projects
Key projects hosted at the Impact Stage under TC oversight include [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: An open protocol enabling integration between LLMs and external data sources and tools.
- **goose**: An extensible open source AI agent runtime.
- **AGENTS.MD**: Standardized repository instruction format for AI agents.

mutations.rationale: Defines the Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide established by the Reference Architectures workstream to assess architectural fit against empirical use cases.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: A methodology and evaluation framework for assessing whether a reference architecture architecturally fits a concrete use case.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide is an evaluation framework and operating guide used to assess whether a given reference architecture (RA) is an appropriate architectural fit for a concrete real-world use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Maintained under the [Reference Architectures Workstream](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration/reference-architectures-workstream.md), the guide provides standardized evaluation criteria for both human contributors and automated coding agents to test and document architectural alignment without requiring premature implementation audits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64], [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification

### Validation Scope and Guarantees

Validation evaluates whether a target use case shares the primary practitioner job and critical system boundaries that the reference architecture is designed to address [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]:

- **Architectural Fit vs. Implementation Audit**: A `Validated` classification indicates that the RA's structure, boundaries, and capability roles fit the use case. It does not certify that an existing system already implements every technical control specified by the RA (such as specific retry policies, credential management, hash checking, or storage mechanisms), as these controls represent architectural requirements provided by the RA for safe operation rather than prerequisites for validation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Evidence Grounding**: Validation assessments must rely strictly on documented evidence from the [Use Case Inventory](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration/critical-use-cases-workstream.md) or primary source references. Illustrative examples embedded within an RA document do not qualify as independent validation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

### Evaluation Process

Validation proceeds through a structured review against the RA's specification:

1. **Checklist & Boundary Comparison**: Compare the RA's checklist, boundaries, guarantees, and exit states against the use case to verify if the RA addresses the core practitioner job [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
2. **Role Allocation**: Map entity responsibilities across the agent, workflow orchestrator, human reviewer, and external integrated systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
3. **Failure and Recovery Paths**: Confirm that the RA accounts for relevant failure handling, waiting, retry loops, human escalation, and handoff boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
4. **Outcome Classification**: Output one of four standardized assessment outcomes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]:
   - `Validated`: The RA provides a complete architectural fit for the job and boundaries.
   - `Partial`: The RA covers substantial portions of the job but leaves critical boundaries unaddressed.
   - `No fit`: The structural requirements or primary job fundamentally diverge from the RA.
   - `Candidate`: Insufficient evidence exists to establish fit, flagging the use case for deeper intake.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architectures Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Workstream within the Workflows & Process Integration WG establishing a catalog of job-oriented reference architectures, patterns, and validation methods.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architectures Workstream is a core initiative within the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../workflows-and-process-integration.md) tasked with authoring, formalizing, and maintaining reusable agentic workflow architectures, composable workflow patterns, and empirical validation methods [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. The workstream operates under the [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](../../specification/job-oriented-architecture-model.md) to structure agentic system designs around recognizable practitioner jobs while isolating sub-problem patterns and empirical validation scenarios [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Architecture / Specification

### Contribution Types

The workstream enforces a clear separation across four distinct contribution types [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:

- **Workflow Patterns**: Independently adoptable solutions addressing a single, recurring workflow sub-problem (e.g., [durable wait](../../specification/durable-wait.md), [human approval gate](../../specification/human-approval-gate.md), or [deterministic acceptance gate](../../specification/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Reference Architectures**: Reusable compositions addressing an entire practitioner job (completing the phrase *“We are building a ___”*), specifying capability roles, boundaries, guarantees, and exit states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Worked Scenarios**: Real or illustrative workflow examples used to validate whether an architecture fits an empirical problem; scenarios do not constitute architectures by themselves [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Decision Notes**: Structured architectural decision records documenting context, trade-offs, and consequences [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

### Authoring Rules and Validation

Contributions across the workstream must adhere to strict neutrality and verification guidelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4], [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]:

- **Vendor Neutrality**: Logical capabilities and boundaries must be described before referencing specific tooling or vendor products [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Explicit Boundaries**: The boundary between agent execution and deterministic workflow-controlled orchestration must be explicitly delineated [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].
- **Evidence Grounding**: Authors must clearly distinguish verified empirical facts from proposed working group interpretations, recording unresolved questions as open questions rather than speculative assertions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4], [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].
- **Use-Case Validation**: Reference architectures are validated against real-world use cases using the [Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide](../../deliverable/ra-use-case-validation-guide.md), evaluating fit and boundary alignment against empirical datasets from the [Critical Use Cases Workstream](critical-use-cases-workstream.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64], [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Defines a reference architecture for resolving a single, bounded problem autonomously using independent acceptance evidence and safe escalation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation architecture serves the job of resolving one small, bounded problem without requiring human approval for every attempt, while preserving clear limits on agent actions and clear evidence for acceptance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It is proposed as a contrasting companion to the [single-agent human approval architecture](../deliverable/single-agent-human-approval-architecture.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
This architecture guarantees bounded autonomy, independent acceptance via a deterministic gate, controlled effect execution, and safe non-convergence [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
This architecture is built from the following workflow patterns: [Bounded convergence loop](../specification/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Deterministic acceptance gate](../specification/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), and [Proposal/execution split](../specification/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
Key components include an Execution Engine, a Bounded Agent Environment, an Isolated or Non-Authoritative Work Area, a Deterministic Acceptance Gate, and a Constrained Effect Executor [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
The architecture requires that the problem is explicitly bounded, an independent deterministic gate can evaluate the result, the permitted effect is constrained, the agent can be fenced, and a safe non-success route is defined [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Lifecycle History
The architecture is currently in draft status for working group review [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. Validation scenarios, such as the Autonomous maintenance run, have been added and reviewed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working group initiative maintaining unified agentic AI taxonomy vocabularies, landscape maps, and defining the terminology lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape group is defined as a cross-working-group **workstream**, not a standalone Working Group (WG) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. It provides a shared review and governance process to ensure AAIF terminology is consistent, useful across groups, and owned by the appropriate WG [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
The workstream is currently focused exclusively on the **Taxonomy**; the **Landscape** remains on the future roadmap [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification
The terminology lifecycle involves five steps: 1. Identify a candidate term; 2. Add it to the candidate spreadsheet (intake and decision log); 3. Decide whether the term qualifies (based on specificity to agentic AI); 4. Draft and socialize the definition; 5. Submit the definition in a pull request [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
Working Groups nominate representatives, known as [Domain Editors](../taxonomy/domain-editor.md), to shepherd terms through this process [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream maintains a roster of Domain Editors from participating WGs, last updated September 3, 2026 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A Domain Editor is a representative nominated by an AAIF Working Group (WG) to participate in the Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
The role involves bringing candidate terms into the workstream, coordinating definition work within their WG, and participating in cross-WG review to ensure terminology consistency [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
